# bazis-permit — guide for AI agents

Permissions for Bazis routes: which objects a user sees and changes, which fields he sees
and writes, which objects a relation may reference. Needs bazis-users. Use it for any API
where users must not see or change everything.

### The sections

Read a section with `package_guide("bazis-permit", "<section>")` when the step at hand
needs it; `guide_search` finds the part of a section that answers a question. A product
with roles needs Model of permissions, Roles in the code, Setup and Rules.

| Section | Read it when |
|---|---|
| Model of permissions | you write the permissions: the slug `<app>.<model>.<item\|field>.<operation>.<selector>…`, the operations, the selectors (`all`, `self`, `author`, a relation, a path), the roles of a user, the roles for anonymous users |
| Roles in the code (`roles.py`) | you declare the roles and the permission groups: `Group`, `Role`, what `migrate` applies, the data migrations, the tests, the checks `permit.E004`, `E005`, `E006`, `W005`, `W006`, `W009`, `W010`, `W011` |
| Setup | you protect a model: the mixins of the user, the anonymous user and the models, `PermitRouteBase`, the 404 and 403 of the items, the check of a created item, the selector arrays, the settings, the users, another route of a protected model, `restrict_queryset` |
| Field permissions | a role must not see or write some fields: `disable`, `readonly`, `enable`, `__all__`, the fields of a list, a field on a create (`add` only with `all`: `field.add.all.all.<field>`, `permit.E006`, `W011`; a required one, `permit.W009`), the fields the filter, sort and search reach |
| Custom actions | an action that is no CRUD: `access_action`, `public`, an aggregate or a report, the actions a user may call (`?meta=custom_actions`), an operation of its own (`AccessAction`) |
| Rules | before you write the code, once: what every route, action and override must respect, the cache of the permissions |

## Model of permissions

User → `roles` (one active: `role_current`) → `Role.groups_permission` →
`GroupPermission.permissions` → `Permission` (a slug):

```
<app>.<model>.<level>.<operation>.<selector>[.<additional>]
entity.document.item.view.org_owner            # documents of the user's organization
entity.document.item.change.author             # documents the user is the author of
entity.meeting.item.view.participants          # meetings the user participates in (m2m)
entity.team.item.view.members                  # the team of the user (reverse of User.team)
entity.meeting.item.view.team__members         # the meetings of the user's team
entity.document.item.view.author=__selector__&is_active=true
entity.document.field.view.all.description.enable
entity.document.field.add.all.name.filter:^[A-Z]+$        # value must match
entity.parent.field.change.all.children.filter:is_active=true  # relation may reference
```

- level `item` (objects) or `field` (fields of objects);
- operations `add` (verified on the created item: its selector and, on a model with
  statuses, its status; see Setup), `view`, `change`, `delete`, `check` (verified on the
  saved item, after triggers filled its selectors) and custom ones;
- selector `all`, `self` (on a model that is itself a `PermitSelectorMixin`: the object
  is the one its `get_selector_for_user(user)` gives, the user himself on a user model,
  `users.user.item.change.self`; a source of several objects, a list or a queryset,
  matches each of them), `author`
  (bazis-author) or a relation linking the object to the user or his selector source
  (`org_owner`: a model that inherits `PermitSelectorMixin` and implements the classmethod
  `get_selector_for_user(user)`, returning an object, a list or a queryset): a foreign key,
  a many-to-many field (`participants`) or a reverse relation by its `related_name`
  (`members` for `User.team = ForeignKey(Team, related_name='members')`, `watchers` for
  `User.teams_watched = ManyToManyField(Team, related_name='watchers')`), or a path of
  relations (`team__members`). A many-to-many or reverse selector matches the objects the
  user is one of the related objects of (an EXISTS subquery: no duplicates); it works for
  the field permissions (`field.view.participants.description.disable`), `check` and
  custom operations such as the transits of bazis-statusy
  (`item.transit.participants.<status>.<transit>`). A custom `through` model needs a unique
  constraint or index on its two foreign keys. A selector that is no such relation matches
  nothing and is logged (`Permit: ... has no selector`).

Roles for anonymous users: `Role(for_anonymous=True)`. Anonymous users never match a
selector other than `all`.

The user model (`UserPermitMixin`) has `roles`, a many-to-many relation to `Role` (its
users: `role.users`), and `role_current`, the active one (`role.users_current`): the
users of a role are `User.objects.filter(roles__slug='manager')`.

The names of `Role` and `GroupPermission` (and of the statuses and transits of
bazis-statusy) are translated fields with the columns `name_en` and `name_ru`, whatever
the languages of the project; `name` reads the column of the active language, else the
first of them in `LANGUAGES`.

## Roles in the code (`roles.py`)

The roles and permission groups of a product are declared in the `roles.py` module of an
application, not in data migrations:

```python
# support/roles.py
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from bazis.contrib.permit.declare import Group, Role

CLIENT = Group('tickets_client', _('Tickets of the client'), [
    'support.ticket.item.view.author.all',          # a model with statuses: .<status>
    'support.ticket.field.view.all.all.assignee.disable',
])
GROUPS = [CLIENT]
ROLES = [Role('client', _('Client'), [CLIENT])]    # groups: Group objects or slugs
```

- `migrate` applies them (`post_migrate`, also sent by `flush`) once all the migrations
  of the project are applied, in one transaction; applied again it writes nothing. The
  declared groups and roles are marked `managed`: the permissions of a managed group and
  the managed groups of a declared role are exactly the declared ones (removed from the
  code = revoked). The groups that are not declared that the admin attached to a declared
  role, and the roles and groups that are not declared, are left; a declared group the
  admin attaches to a declared role that does not list it is removed. A declared slug that
  exists unmarked is taken over with a warning in the log, and from then on synced: its
  permissions (or managed groups) that are not declared are revoked. A managed object no
  longer declared is kept (`permit.W006`) and is an ordinary object in the admin again.
  Concurrent `migrate` runs apply them one after the other (a PostgreSQL advisory lock).
- A data migration of the product runs before the declarations are applied (they are
  applied after the last migration): on a fresh database it cannot rely on the declared
  roles or groups.
- Names: English msgids (`gettext_lazy`); `name_en`/`name_ru` get the translations of the
  catalogs of the project (`manage.py bazis_messages status` lists the untranslated ones;
  `permit.W004` is removed in bazis-permit 2.11).
- The admin shows declared objects read-only (a declared role still takes groups of the
  admin) and does not delete them.
- Tests: the test database is migrated (also with `--reuse-db`: Django still runs
  `migrate` on the kept database), so the declarations are there; a test with
  `transaction=True` gets them back after the flush. `bazis_test_utils` gives
  `apply_declarations()` and the fixture `bazis_declared`, for a test that changes the
  declared rows itself.
- `bazis.contrib.permit.declare.apply_declarations(using, groups=None, roles=None,
  dry_run=False)` returns the changes; `dry_run` only lists them.
- Checks: `permit.E004` (a slug, a duplicate, a group of a role that is not declared),
  `permit.E005` (a permission: grammar, the model is a `PermitModelMixin`, the selector is
  a relation to a `PermitSelectorMixin` model, the field exists, the restriction is one of
  the schemas of the core, `enable`/`disable`/`readonly`/`writeonly`, `required`/`optional`,
  `nullable`/`notnull`, `blank`/`notblank`, or `filter:`), `permit.E006` (a field
  permission of `add` with a selector or a status other than `all` that restricts its
  field, `disable`, `readonly`, `required`, `notnull`, `notblank` or `filter:`: it never
  applies and the restriction is lost, see Field permissions), `permit.W011` (a warning:
  such a permission that only relaxes its field, `enable`, `writeonly`, `optional`,
  `nullable` or `blank`, which leaves the create stricter than declared),
  `permit.W009` (`bazis_doctor`: a `disable` on
  add of a required field, which the create schema keeps, see Field permissions); with a
  database (`bazis_doctor` from bazis 2.13, against the database it reaches; with an older core only
  `manage.py check --database default`) `permit.W005` (the database differs: migrate),
  `permit.W006` (orphans) and `permit.W010` (a field permission of `add` with a condition
  that a role of the database has, made in the admin or the API: the roles and the slug).
  These are warnings: `migrate` runs the database checks before it applies the
  declarations.

## Setup

```python
from bazis.contrib.permit.models_abstract import (
    AnonymousUserPermitMixin, PermitModelMixin, PermitSelectorMixin, UserPermitMixin,
)
from bazis.contrib.permit.routes_abstract import PermitRouteBase

# users/models.py: the user is the source of the `author` selector (PermitSelectorMixin),
# the anonymous user gets the roles for anonymous users
class User(UserPermitMixin, PermitSelectorMixin, UuidMixin, UserAbstract, JsonApiMixin):
    pass

class AnonymousUser(AnonymousUserPermitMixin, AnonymousUserAbstract):
    pass

class Document(PermitModelMixin, AuthorMixin, DtMixin, UuidMixin, JsonApiMixin):
    autogen_selectors_fields = ['author']    # selector fields with GIN indexes
    ...

class DocumentRouteSet(PermitRouteBase):
    model = apps.get_model('docs.Document')
```

- `BS_INSTALLED_APPS` includes `bazis.contrib.permit`; register `bazis.contrib.permit.router`
  for the roles, groups and permissions API.
- `PermitRouteBase` filters the querysets, hides fields, builds the schemas per user, checks
  every CRUD action and the relationships endpoints, and adds the meta fields
  `for_change`, `for_delete`, `for_create`, `crud_actions`, `custom_actions` (requested
  with `?meta=`, see Custom actions).
- Anonymous users can only read (create, update and delete are 403; update and delete
  of an item they cannot view 404), within the roles marked `for_anonymous`.
- An item the user cannot view does not exist for him: the routes of an item (retrieve,
  update, delete, the relationships endpoints, `schema_retrieve`, `schema_update`, the
  transits of bazis-statusy) look the item up among the objects he views
  (`PermitRouteBase.get_queryset_for_item`, `restrict_queryset` for `view` in the same
  query) and answer the 404 of the core for a missing item, the same detail and queries;
  an item he views but cannot change or delete is 403. The read of the response after a
  write is not restricted: a create or an update that makes the item invisible is 403 and
  rolled back; a statusy transit that hides it is kept and answers 204.
- **A created item matches an `item.add` permission** (bazis-permit 2.11): the create
  schema is built when the user has any `item.add` permission on the model (`for_create`
  says the same), then the created item, also an included one (by the permissions of its
  own model), is checked against their selectors and, on a model with statuses, their
  status: `item.add.author` (the author is set by the server: every create matches),
  `item.add.participants` (the user must be among the participants the document sets),
  `item.add.team__members` (the team of the user), `item.add.all.draft` (only in `draft`).
  An item that matches none is 403 `ERR_FORBIDDEN` and the request is rolled back. The
  item is checked as created: saved, with its to-many relations and the values the server
  filled (`hook_before_create`, the triggers), in `PermitRouteBase.hook_after_create`, before
  the after-create effects of the route: an override of `hook_after_create` calls `super()`
  first, so what it changes afterwards (an automatic transit) is the server's, not the
  user's. A selector the new item cannot match (a reverse relation nobody links yet)
  refuses every create of the role. Each item is checked right after its own insert, the
  main item first, then the included ones in the order of the document: a selector of an
  item that only an item created later in the same request would satisfy (a reverse
  relation the included items fill) refuses the create, too strict but never a bypass;
  create such items in two requests. An included item of a model whose default route is
  no `PermitRouteBase` is checked by the permission service of the route of the request.
  A permission without a condition (`item.add.all`, `item.add.all.all`) allows every item
  without a query. An update is not checked against `add` (its result: `check`). Code
  that writes through the ORM (a command, the admin, `transit_apply`) is not checked.
- **Effects of a create that a refusal does not undo.** The check runs in
  `hook_after_create` of `PermitRouteBase`, after `hook_before_create` and the insert, and
  a refusal rolls back the transaction of the request only: what runs before it and does
  not live in the database transaction (a task of bazis-bg queued without
  `transaction.on_commit`, a call of an external service, a mail, a signal handler with
  such effects) has happened anyway. Put such effects behind `transaction.on_commit`, or in
  `hook_after_create` after `super()`. A mixin whose `hook_after_create` comes before
  `PermitRouteBase` in the bases of the route set runs its code after the check only if it
  calls `super()` first: list the mixins with effects after `PermitRouteBase`, or call
  `super()` first in them.
- Selector array fields (`autogen_<field>_selectors`, GIN) are generated only for the
  forward relations to `PermitSelectorMixin` models listed in `autogen_selectors_fields`;
  many-to-many and reverse selectors do not need them. An array holds ids of selector
  objects that the permissions of the selector also match (a delegate of the author: the
  project fills it, or the admin); it is not in the schemas of the routes
  (`get_fields_hidden`, bazis-permit 2.11 with bazis 2.16), so the `fields` of a route do
  not exclude it and a client cannot write it.
- Custom actions (routes of kind `other` of the `http_*` decorators, see below) check the
  permission they declare (`access_action`), else are closed to anonymous users unless
  `public=True`.
- Settings: `BS_BAZIS_PERMISSION_CACHE_EXPIRE` (seconds, 7; dynamic, in the admin) and
  the deprecated `BS_BAZIS_PERMIT_RELATIONS_VIEW_CHECK` (`permit.W001`).
- A selector source (`client` of `service.act.field.change.client.…`, `Act.client =
  ForeignKey(Client)`): the model
  inherits `PermitSelectorMixin` and implements the classmethod
  `get_selector_for_user(user)`; a false value (no client) makes the permission match
  nothing:

  ```python
  class Client(PermitSelectorMixin, ...):
      @classmethod
      def get_selector_for_user(cls, user):
          return user.client          # an object, a list or a queryset; None: nothing
  ```
- The users: the routes of bazis-users do not check permissions (`permit.W002` lists
  them). To restrict them, the user model also inherits `PermitModelMixin` (else
  `permit.W003`) and the project registers its own route set of it, a `PermitRouteBase`
  (`default_route = True`), instead of the router of bazis-users.
- Another route of a protected model (a projection every user sees, a calendar) may be a
  route without permissions (`UserRequiredRouteBase` of bazis-users): its list and items
  are its `get_queryset`, and the relationships, `included` and filters of the other
  routes still use `restrict_queryset` of the default route (the `PermitRouteBase`; declare
  `default_route = True` on it). `permit.W002` reports it; `permit_public = True` on the
  route only says that its data is public and silences the warning, it changes nothing
  else.
- A route that restricts its objects by a rule of its own overrides `restrict_queryset`
  (of `RestrictedQsRouteMixin`) and applies it in its `get_queryset` (the core does not
  apply it to the list and items of the route): `permit.W002` skips it (bazis-permit
  2.10), with no `permit_public`. So are the routes of bazis-uploadable (the files of the
  user) and bazis-bg (the tasks of the user) and their subclasses. The check sees only
  the override, not that `get_queryset` uses it.
- To see more objects, add a permission (another selector), not code. An override of
  `restrict_queryset` keeps the permissions and narrows them:

  ```python
  @class_or_instance_method      # bazis.core.utils.functools
  def restrict_queryset(self, qs, access_action, user=None, permit=None, **kwargs):
      qs = super().restrict_queryset(qs, access_action, user=user, permit=permit, **kwargs)
      return qs.exclude(is_archived=True)
  ```

  (the queryset of bazis-permit also carries the field groups of its objects).

## Field permissions

Field permissions restrict the fields of the objects a permission of the item matches,
per operation (`view`, `add`, `change`) and selector:

- **Hide, protect, show.** `field.view.<selector>.<field>.disable` removes the field from
  the data of the objects the selector matches; `field.change.<selector>.<field>.readonly`
  marks it `readOnly: true` in `schema_update` of the item (the attributes schema in
  `$defs`), an update ignores it (200, the value unchanged) and its relationships
  endpoints answer 403 `ERR_RELATIONSHIP_READONLY` (bazis 2.8.1; a 500 before).
  `__all__` in place of the field is every field of the schema; a restriction of the
  field itself replaces the one of `__all__` of the same kind (availability: `enable`,
  `readonly`, `disable`), and of the permissions of the user that match an object,
  `enable` wins over `readonly` and `disable`, and `readonly` over `disable`. One field
  writable, the others read-only (a model with statuses has the status segment,
  `client.all.__all__.readonly`):

  ```python
  'service.act.field.change.client.__all__.readonly',
  'service.act.field.change.client.confirmed.enable',
  ```
- **The fields of a list.** An object of a list has the fields of its card (bazis-permit
  2.11): up to 4 conditional field groups (other selectors or statuses) of a role on a
  model (`FIELD_GROUPS_COMBINED_MAX`, a schema per combination, at most 16); with more,
  the list shows every object with the fields shown in all of them (the card shows more),
  so keep the conditions of a role few. The first member of `schema_list` (`anyOf[0]` of
  `data.items`) is the union of the fields some object of the list may show, the columns
  of a client; no object has it. The members are the combinations an object the user
  views may match: when the condition of each of his view permissions is that of a
  conditional field group (`item.view.all.open` with
  `field.view.all.open.__all__.disable`, a role for anonymous users), a combination
  without these groups is left out, and the union names only the fields of the open
  objects. The conditions are compared as written, not by what they imply: with a view
  permission of another condition (or none) the union may name a field that no object
  the user views shows (its name, never a value).
- **On add, a field permission takes no condition: `field.add.all.all.<field>`.** The create
  schema is built before the object exists, so its selector and status are not known (the
  CREATE schema of a model with statuses accepts an initial `status`). A field permission
  of `add` applies only with the selector `all` and, on a model with statuses, the status
  `all`: `field.add.all.all.<field>.disable` (without statuses `field.add.all.<field>.disable`)
  hides the field from every create of the role. `field.add.all.draft.<field>.disable` (the
  initial status too), `field.add.author.<field>.disable` and any other condition never
  apply: `roles.py` refuses them (`permit.E006`, the hint names the slug to write;
  `enable` and the other restrictions that only relax the field are the warning
  `permit.W011`), `bazis_doctor` reports those of the database (`permit.W010`); before
  bazis-permit 2.11 they did nothing without a word. The `view` and `change` permissions
  keep their selector and status (`field.change.all.draft.price.readonly`). To restrict
  which objects a role creates, use the item permissions of add: `item.add.<selector>`
  (`.<status>`) is checked on the created item (see Setup).
- **A required field cannot be hidden from a create.** `disable` on `add` hides a field
  from the create schema only when it is optional: a field required to create an item (a
  model field without `blank=True`, `null=True` or a default) stays in the create schema
  of the role, so `field.add.all.<field>.disable` changes nothing and a create
  without the field is 422 `ERR_VALIDATE` "Field required" at it. A field the server fills
  (the creator, the owner): make the model field optional (`blank=True`, `null=True` or a
  default), set it in `hook_before_create` of the route (call `super()`), then disable it
  for the role. `bazis_doctor` warns of such a declaration in `roles.py` (`permit.W009`).
  `disable` on `change` hides a field from the update schema whatever its requiredness in
  the model (bazis 2.16): an update with it is 422, its relationships endpoints answer 403
  `ERR_RELATIONSHIP_READONLY`. The one exception: `<field>.required` keeps the field
  against `__all__.disable` (the permission names it); the field's own `disable` always
  wins, also over its own `required` from another group of the user. Before bazis 2.16 a
  field required in the model stayed in the update schema and an update changed it: there
  declare `readonly` on `change`.
- **The filter, the sorting and the search.** With Bazis 2.9 the `filter`, `sort` and
  `search` of a request reach only the fields the field permissions show the user in
  every object: `PermitRouteBase.query_fields(user=None,
  **kwargs)` (bazis-permit 2.11; before, any field shown in some object, and every field
  when an object could match no field permission). A field hidden in some objects, also
  only in those of a status or a selector the user cannot view, is 400 `ERR_FILTER` (also
  through a relation, `meetings__description`) and left out of the search, so its values
  cannot be found by trial; the conditions are not compared with those of `item.view`.
  A public subset of the fields (a role for anonymous users that views the open objects)
  restricts the fields under the condition of the view; the fields it enables are shown
  and filterable, the others neither:

  ```python
  'jobs.vacancy.item.view.all.open',
  'jobs.vacancy.field.view.all.open.__all__.disable',
  'jobs.vacancy.field.view.all.open.title.enable',   # title: shown and filterable
  ```

  A field shown in every object the user views but hidden in a status he cannot view
  (`field.view.all.archived.salary.disable` with `item.view.all.open`) is not filterable
  either: limit such a rule to the roles that view that status. The internal conditions of the
  permissions (`QueryToOrm` of selectors, `filter:` restrictions) are not restricted.

## Custom actions

A custom action of a `PermitRouteBase` (a route of kind `other`: the `http_*` decorators
without `kind=`, not `http_internal`; the CRUD, relationships and schema routes check
themselves) declares who may call it (bazis-permit 2.11 with bazis 2.16). bazis-permit
checks it in `route_check`, before the action runs, in its transaction:

```python
from bazis.core.routes_abstract.initial import http_get, http_post
from bazis.core.schemas.enums import CrudAccessAction
from bazis.core.throttle import throttle

class CertificateRouteSet(PermitRouteBase):
    model = apps.get_model('training.Certificate')

    @http_get('/export/', access_action=CrudAccessAction.VIEW)     # the collection
    def action_export(self, **kwargs):
        qs = self.restrict_queryset(self.model.objects.all(), CrudAccessAction.VIEW)
        ...

    @http_post('/{item_id}/revoke/', access_action=CrudAccessAction.CHANGE)  # an item
    def action_revoke(self, item_id: str, **kwargs):
        item = self.set_item(item_id, with_lock=True)   # checked and locked already
        ...

    @http_get('/{item_id}/card/', public=False)          # any authenticated user
    def action_card(self, item_id: str, **kwargs):
        return self.set_item(item_id).title              # among the items he views

    @http_get('/verify/', public=True, dependencies=[throttle('10/minute', key='ip')])
    def action_verify(self, code: str, **kwargs):        # anyone
        ...
```

- `public=True`: anyone, also anonymous users, without a check; limited by
  `BAZIS_THROTTLE_PUBLIC` (`'30/minute'` per user or IP address, dynamic; empty:
  unlimited) unless it declares its own `throttle` (core guide). Restrict what it returns
  yourself. A public action of an item that takes its item with `set_item` still looks it
  up among the objects the (anonymous) user views.
- `access_action=CrudAccessAction.<X>` (or `StatusyAccessAction.TRANSIT`, ...): the roles
  decide, also the roles for anonymous users (`Role(for_anonymous=True)`). An action of the
  collection (no `{item_id}` in the path) needs the permission on the model (403). An action
  of an item: bazis-permit takes the item of `item_id` into `self.item` before the action
  runs (404 for an item the user cannot view) and checks the permission on it (403). For a
  method that writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) it takes it locked (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE`,
  until the end of the request), so the permission checked (by a selector or a status of
  the item) holds while the action runs; `self.set_item(item_id, with_lock=True)` then
  returns it without another query. A GET action that needs the lock calls
  `set_item(item_id, with_lock=True)` (the item is read again, locked; the permission was
  checked before the action on the unlocked item, so a GET action must not rely on a
  permission that depends on fields another request may change meanwhile). The core `/_id/` route declares `access_action=view`: open as `GET /`.
- **An aggregate or a report** (a count, a funnel, a time to close, an export):
  `access_action=CrudAccessAction.VIEW` lets everyone who can view the model call it, the
  roles for anonymous users and the narrowest role that views an object among them, and
  the action returns what its code computes, not what each of them may see. Give it an
  operation of its own (`REPORT`, below) granted only to the roles that may see the
  report, and compute it over the objects the user views, by the `restrict_queryset` of
  the default route of their model with the user of the request; `permit.W008`
  (`bazis_doctor`) reports an action whose `access_action` a role for anonymous users
  has (for an action of an item, with `all` or a condition he may match, also an
  alternative such as `author=__selector__|is_public=true`):

  ```python
  @http_get('/{item_id}/funnel/', access_action=VacancyAccessAction.REPORT)
  def action_funnel(self, item_id: str, **kwargs):
      visible = ApplicationRouteSet.restrict_queryset(
          Application.objects.all(), CrudAccessAction.VIEW, user=self.inject.user)
      # the candidates of the vacancy the user views, not all of them
      qs = Application.objects.filter(vacancy=self.item, pk__in=visible.values('pk'))
      return dict(qs.values_list('stage').annotate(total=Count('id')))

  # jobs/roles.py: the recruiter of the vacancy and the managers, not the guest
  'jobs.vacancy.item.report.recruiter',
  'jobs.vacancy.item.report.all',
  ```

  An action anonymous users may call is `public=True`.
- Neither (or `public=False`): authenticated users only, anonymous ones get 403
  `ERR_FORBIDDEN` (as on a create or an update), whatever their roles. Without a
  declaration `permit.W007` warns, for an action of the collection and of an item: declare
  `access_action`, or `public=False` when any authenticated user may call it (an action of
  an item that takes its item with `set_item` only among the items he views). Check any
  other operation explicitly: `self.check_access(CrudAccessAction.CHANGE, item)` (403).
- An override that does not repeat `public`/`access_action` keeps those of the route it
  overrides (as `kind`); `route_declare(route, public=True)` (core) changes them on an
  inherited route without repeating its decorator. `x-bazis` in OpenAPI shows `public`
  (always) and `access_action` (when declared).
- **Which actions the user may call** (to show the buttons of a client): the meta field
  `custom_actions` (bazis-permit 2.11), requested with `?meta=custom_actions` (with
  others: `?meta=crud_actions,custom_actions`), lists the names of the actions (`action`
  of `x-bazis` in OpenAPI, e.g. `action_revoke`) the user may call by the rule above
  (`PermitRouteBase.action_allowed`, the one `route_check` enforces): on an item (retrieve,
  and the response of a create, an update or a transit) the actions of an item on this
  item, on a list the actions of the collection; only the routes the route set registers
  (`actions`/`actions_exclude`). A check the action makes in its own code (the transits
  of bazis-statusy: `state_actions`) is not part of it. Do not write a meta field of your
  own for it.

  ```
  GET /api/v1/training/certificate/<id>/?meta=crud_actions,custom_actions
  "meta": {"crud_actions": ["view", "change"], "custom_actions": ["action_card", "action_revoke"]}
  GET /api/v1/training/certificate/?meta=custom_actions
  "meta": {"custom_actions": ["action_export", "action_list_id", "action_verify"]}
  ```
- **An operation of its own** (a permission no CRUD operation expresses: export the
  participants, revoke): a subclass of `AccessAction` (core) whose value is the operation
  of the permission slug. Any operation name is valid in a slug; a model with statuses has
  the status segment after the selector, as for the CRUD operations:

  ```python
  # training/access.py
  from bazis.core.schemas.enums import AccessAction

  class CertificateAccessAction(AccessAction):
      REPORT = 'report'        # training.certificate.item.report.<selector>[.<status>]

  # training/routes.py
  @http_post('/{item_id}/report/', access_action=CertificateAccessAction.REPORT)
  def action_report(self, item_id: str, **kwargs): ...

  # training/roles.py: the roles that may call it
  'training.certificate.item.report.author',
  ```

  Check it in code with `self.check_access(CertificateAccessAction.REPORT, item)` (403).

## Rules

- Every route of a protected model inherits `PermitRouteBase` or restricts its objects
  with its own `restrict_queryset` (`permit.W002` lists the JSON:API routes that do
  neither). Only a route of public data declares `permit_public = True`.
- Every custom action declares `access_action` or `public` (`permit.W007`); an action open
  to anonymous users is `public=True`, and an action closed to them needs no check of
  `is_anonymous` in its code. An aggregate or a report has an operation of its own
  (`AccessAction`), not `CrudAccessAction.VIEW`, which every role that views the model
  has, the roles for anonymous users among them (`permit.W008`).
- A create is checked against the selector and the status of the `item.add` permissions on
  each created item right after its insert (403 and rolled back): an override of
  `hook_after_create` calls `super()` first; do not check the selector of a create
  yourself. Effects of a create outside the database (tasks, external calls, mails) go
  behind `transaction.on_commit`: a refused create does not undo them (see Setup).
- The model of a `PermitRouteBase` route is a `PermitModelMixin` (a `PermitStructMixin`):
  with another model the route and the relations into it fail with `AttributeError` as
  soon as the user has a permission on the model (`permit.W003`, a warning).
- The core (Bazis 2.7) lets an item reference only the objects the user can view (a
  reverse relation: link and unlink only the objects he can change), and `included` shows
  only the objects he can view, by `restrict_queryset` of the default route of the related
  model (`PermitRouteBase` for a protected model). Do not check the related objects
  yourself; `relation_targets_check = False` turns it off for a route. A route without a
  user (not a `UserRouteBase`) is checked as for an anonymous user unless the request user
  is in `UserMixin.CTX_USER_REQUEST`.
- `BS_BAZIS_PERMIT_RELATIONS_VIEW_CHECK` and `relations_view_check` are deprecated (no
  effect; `relations_view_check = False` works as `relation_targets_check = False`) and
  will be removed in 3.0; `permit.W001` reports the setting.
- Override `restrict_queryset(qs, access_action, user=None, permit=None, **kwargs)` with
  `**kwargs`: the core calls it on the class.
- A field the field permissions hide from a user in some of the objects he views is not
  filterable, sortable or searchable for him (see Field permissions).
- Permissions are cached per user for `BAZIS_PERMISSION_CACHE_EXPIRE` seconds and
  invalidated when roles, groups or permissions change through the ORM (`save`, `delete`,
  m2m); `QuerySet.update()` and `bulk_create()` do not invalidate the cache.

agents_md:
# bazis-statusy — guide for AI agents

Statuses of objects and transitions between them (workflows): transitions (`Transit`) are
configured per model as data, run validators and actions that are methods of the model, and
are permissions of bazis-permit. Needs bazis-permit (and so bazis-users).

### The sections

Read a section with `package_guide("bazis-statusy", "<section>")` when the step at hand
needs it; `guide_search` finds the part of a section that answers a question. A model with
a workflow needs Setup, Workflows in the code, Validators, actions and the payload, and
Rules.

| Section | Read it when |
|---|---|
| Setup | you give a model statuses: `StatusyMixin`, `StatusyRouteSetBase`, the migrations, the initial status, the public catalog router, the permissions by status, the status of a create (`statusy.W005`, `W006`) |
| Workflows in the code (`workflow.py`) | you declare the statuses and transits of a model: `Workflow`, `Status`, `Transit`, `initial=`, what `migrate` applies, the checks `statusy.E001`–`E004`, `W003`, `W004` |
| Validators, actions and the payload | you write the methods of a transit: `transit_validator`, `transit_before`, `transit_after`, `TransitError`, the payload type, a required text, the titles of its fields |
| API of a StatusyRouteSetBase route | a client makes a transit: `POST /{item_id}/transit/` and its answers, `schema_transit`, a transit for anonymous users, the meta `state_actions`, `for_transit`, `status_aggs`, `GET /{item_id}/status_history/` |
| Transits in code and the history | the code makes a transit: `get_transit`, `transit_apply` and its payload, the actor of a system transit, an automatic transit on create, the history and `status_history` |
| Rules | before you write the code, once: the status changes only by transits, the routes, `StatusyChildMixin` and the validation of the children, `validate_item` on a transit |
| Statuses and transits as data | the statuses and transits are rows made in the admin or a data migration: `Status`, `Transit`, `StatusyContentType` |

## Setup

```python
from bazis.contrib.statusy import TransitError, transit_after, transit_before, transit_validator
from bazis.contrib.statusy.models_abstract import StatusyMixin, StatusyTransit, TransitBase
from bazis.contrib.statusy.routes_abstract import StatusyRouteSetBase
from bazis.contrib.statusy.schemas import payload_validate_none
from bazis.core.schemas import CrudApiAction, SchemaFields

class Order(StatusyMixin, DtMixin, UuidMixin, JsonApiMixin):
    is_paid = models.BooleanField(default=False)

    @transit_validator('Order is paid')            # the label shown in the admin
    def validator_paid(self, transit: TransitBase, user, payload):
        if not self.is_paid:
            raise TransitError('The order is not paid')

    @transit_before('Set the date')    # ClosePayload: a Pydantic model, the payload is required
    def before_date(self, statusy_transit: StatusyTransit, payload: ClosePayload):
        self.dt_closed = payload.dt_closed
        self.save()

class OrderRouteSet(StatusyRouteSetBase):
    model = apps.get_model('shop.Order')
```

- `BS_INSTALLED_APPS` includes `bazis.contrib.permit`, `bazis.contrib.statusy` and
  `translated_fields`. Run `makemigrations`: `StatusyMixin` adds `status`, `status_dt`,
  `status_author` and a history model `<Model>StatusyTransit` in the same app
  (`item.statusy_transits`).
- The initial status of new objects is `Workflow(initial=...)` of the model (see Workflows
  in the code), else `BAZIS_STATUS_INITIAL` (default `["draft", "Draft"]`,
  `BS_BAZIS_STATUS_INITIAL='["new", "New"]'`, for all the models); its `Status` row is
  created on first use.
- The statuses and transits of a model are declared in `workflow.py` (see Workflows in the
  code); rows made in the admin or a data migration: see Statuses and transits as data.
- Optionally `router.register('bazis.contrib.statusy.router')`: the read-only statuses and
  transits of every workflow, a public catalog (`permit_public = True`, no `permit.W002`
  since 2.12.0). Registering it publishes the workflow of all the models with statuses to
  every user, anonymous ones included: `statusy/status/` (`id`, `name`) and
  `statusy/transit/` (`id`, `name`, `hint`, `hint_title`, `hint_action`, `model`,
  `status_src`, `status_dst`; not the methods, `source_link`, `is_schema_validate` or
  `transits_related`). Register it if a client names the statuses and transits by their
  ids; leave it out if the workflow must not be public.
- **Permissions by status.** On a statusy model the item permissions take the status of
  the object after the selector (`all` or a status id); a transit is the operation
  `transit` with the transit id last:

  ```
  shop.order.item.view.all.all
  shop.order.item.add.all.draft                    # create only in `draft`
  shop.order.item.change.author.draft              # change only in `draft`
  shop.order.item.transit.author.draft.to_paid     # transit `to_paid` from `draft`
  ```

- **The status of a create.** The CREATE schema accepts an initial `status` (omitted: the
  initial status of the model), and bazis-permit (2.11) checks the created item against
  the `item.add` permissions of the user, the status segment literally: with
  `item.add.all.draft` a create without `status`, or with `draft`, is allowed, one with
  `paid` is 403 `ERR_FORBIDDEN` (nothing written); `item.add.all.paid` creates only with
  `paid` sent, a create without `status` (`draft`) is 403; `item.add.all.all` creates in any
  status the client sends, skipping the transits, their validators, actions and
  permissions. Name the statuses a role creates in. To take the choice away from every
  client, exclude the field: `CrudApiAction.CREATE: SchemaFields(exclude={'status': None})`
  on the route; every create then gets the initial status, which the add permissions must
  name (or `all`). `bazis_doctor` warns of a role whose add permissions on a model name
  neither its initial status nor `all` (`statusy.W005`: every create without `status` is
  refused) and of `item.add.<selector>.all` while a route of the model accepts `status`
  on a create and the role does not hide it (`statusy.W006`), for the roles of `roles.py`
  and those of the database (with the database checks). To take the choice away from one
  role only, hide the field from its creates: `shop.order.field.add.all.all.status.disable`
  (a create with it is 422) or `readonly` (a create ignores it). A status that is not one of the workflow of the model is
  not refused by the permission `all`; a status that does not exist is 422 `ERR_VALIDATE`
  at `/data/relationships/status/data/id` (bazis 2.16; a 500 before).

## Workflows in the code (`workflow.py`)

The statuses and transits of a product are declared in the `workflow.py` module of an
application (needs bazis-permit 2.9: its roles are declared the same way in `roles.py`),
not in data migrations:

```python
# shop/workflow.py
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from bazis.contrib.statusy.declare import Status, Transit, Workflow

DRAFT, PAID = Status('draft', _('Draft')), Status('paid', _('Paid'))
WORKFLOWS = [
    Workflow('shop.Order', [DRAFT, PAID], [
        Transit('to_paid', _('Pay'), DRAFT, PAID,
                validators=['validator_paid'], actions_before=['before_date']),
    ], initial=DRAFT),
]
```

- `initial=` (a status of the workflow or its id) is the status of a new object of the
  model that is created without one (the API, `Order()`, `Order.objects.create()`; a loaded
  object or an explicit `status` is kept), instead of the global `BAZIS_STATUS_INITIAL`
  (bazis-statusy 2.12). The admin form of a new object still starts with the global
  default: pick the status there. An initial status that is not a status of the workflow
  is `statusy.E001`. `initial_status(Model)` of `bazis.contrib.statusy.declare` reads it
  (None without one), as the contract of bazis-front does.

- `migrate` applies them (`post_migrate`, also sent by `flush`) once all the migrations
  of the project are applied, in one transaction; applied again it writes nothing. The
  statuses are shared by the models (one name per id); the transits of a declared model
  get the declared name, statuses and methods (the other fields, `hint`,
  `is_schema_validate`, `transits_related`, stay as the admin set them). The cached
  content types (`ContentType`, `StatusyContentType`) are forgotten first: `flush` makes
  them again with other ids.
- Nothing is deleted: a status (its objects would be deleted, `on_delete=CASCADE`) nor a
  transit of a declared model that is not declared (its history, the transit facts of the
  objects, would be deleted): `statusy.W004` lists such transits. A declared transit id
  that is a transit of another model in the database stops `migrate` (`statusy.E004`).
- A data migration of the product runs before the declarations are applied (they are
  applied after the last migration): on a fresh database it cannot rely on the declared
  statuses or transits.
- Names: English msgids (`gettext_lazy`) translated into `name_en`/`name_ru` by the
  catalogs of the project (`manage.py bazis_messages status` lists the untranslated ones;
  `statusy.W002` is removed in bazis-statusy 2.12).
- Tests: the test database is migrated, so the workflows are there, also after the flush
  of a test with `transaction=True`; `bazis_test_utils` gives `apply_declarations()` and
  the fixture `bazis_declared`.
- `bazis.contrib.statusy.declare.apply_declarations(using, workflows=None, dry_run=False)`
  returns the changes; `dry_run` only lists them.
- Checks: `statusy.E001` (the model is a `StatusyMixin`, one workflow per model, the ids,
  a transit between statuses of its workflow, a transit id unique among the models, one
  name per status, the initial status is one of the workflow), `statusy.E002` (a validator or action that is not a method of the
  model), `statusy.E003` (a permission of `roles.py` of a model with a declared workflow
  names a status that is not one of the workflow, a transit that is not declared for the
  model, or a status the transit does not start from); with a database
  (`bazis_doctor` from bazis 2.13, against the database it reaches; with an older core
  only `manage.py check --database default`) `statusy.W003` (the database differs:
  migrate), `statusy.W004` and `statusy.E004` (a declared transit id is a transit of
  another model).

## Validators, actions and the payload

The methods are listed by name in the `Transit`; `transit_apply` (and so the endpoint)
calls them with these signatures:

```python
@transit_validator('Label')   # (self, transit, user, payload): raise to refuse
def validator_x(self, transit: TransitBase, user, payload: XPayload): ...

@transit_before('Label')      # (self, statusy_transit, payload): before the status is set
def before_x(self, statusy_transit: StatusyTransit, payload: XPayload): ...

@transit_after('Label')       # (self, statusy_transit, payload): after the status is set
def after_x(self, statusy_transit: StatusyTransit, payload): ...
```

- A validator raises `TransitError('...')` (or `JsonApiBazisException`, a pydantic
  `ValidationError`): the errors of all the validators are collected and answered together
  with 422 (`TransitError` is `ERR_TRANSIT`).
  `user` is the user of the transit (None for a system transit). A validator is also called
  with `payload is payload_validate_none` to build the `restricts` of `state_actions`:
  return early then, before reading the payload.
- An action gets the history record `statusy_transit` (its `transit`, `author`, `extra`;
  saved, the status not yet set for a before action) and the payload object. A before
  action saves the changes of the item itself (`self.save()`); if it returns an object, the
  next actions run on it and `transit_apply` returns it (read again). The return of an after
  action is ignored. All
  of it runs in one transaction with the history record.
- **The payload type** comes from the annotations of the parameter `payload` of the
  validators and the actions of the transit: each annotation is a pydantic model, and the
  transit's payload type is one model inheriting all of them: the payload type is
  `Model.get_transit_payload_type(transit)`, a classmethod (it does not depend on an
  object): override it; `item.transit_payload_type(transit)` is the same under its old
  name. The client sends one `payload` object with the fields of all the models, it
  is validated as a whole (422 with an error per invalid field, 400 `This transition
  requires a payload` when it is missing), and every method receives that
  same object. A `payload` without an annotation adds nothing; a transit whose methods have
  no annotated `payload` has no payload type, the methods receive None. A model with a
  classmethod `schema_build(transit)` returns the model to use for each transit.
- **A required text of the payload** (a reason of a rejection): `reason: str =
  Field(title=_('Reason'), min_length=1, max_length=2000)`. The payload type strips the
  texts of its fields before their length is checked (bazis-statusy 2.12): a reason of
  only spaces is refused (422 at `/payload/reason`) and the methods receive the stripped
  text; do not strip it again in an action. A model nested in the payload keeps its own
  configuration (`model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` to strip its
  texts). Test the transit with a text of only spaces.
- **The titles of the payload fields**: `Field(title=_('Reason'))` with `gettext_lazy`,
  kept lazy: the JSON schemas of the payload (the body of the transit in `state_actions`,
  the contract of bazis-front) are generated in the language of the request (of the export)
  by `TranslatedJsonSchema` of the core (`bazis.core.utils.schemas`, bazis 2.14: the
  payload type and the transit body are `TranslatedSchemaModel`).
  Do not wrap it in `str()`: the title would keep the language of the process start.
  Without a title, pydantic derives it from the field name (`must_active` → `Must Active`).

## API of a StatusyRouteSetBase route

- `POST /{item_id}/transit/` with the plain JSON body (not a JSON:API document)
  `{"transit": "<transit id>", "payload": {...}}` (`payload` omitted or null for a transit
  without a payload type, see below): 200 with the item (204 if the user can no longer view it); 403 if the user has no permission for
  the transit or it does not start from the current status (from bazis-permit 2.8.0, 404
  for an item the user cannot view, as for a missing one); 400 without a required
  payload; 422 with the errors of the payload and the validators. An action of bazis-permit
  declared `public=False` (bazis-statusy 2.12): authenticated users only, an anonymous user
  gets 403 even with a transit permission of a role for anonymous users, unless a route
  declares it again with `public=True` (below).
- `GET /{item_id}/schema_transit/`: the schema the object must satisfy before a transit with
  `is_schema_validate` (default true); kind `schema` in `x-bazis` (bazis-statusy 2.12).
- `GET /{item_id}/status_history/` (bazis-statusy 2.15): the history of the item, below
  (The history in the API). Kind `other` in `x-bazis`, `access_action` `history`: the permission
  `shop.order.item.history.<selector>.<status>` (like `transit`), granted by the roles that
  may read the history; the item must be visible too.
- A transit for anonymous users (a guest request, a public form): a route of its own that
  declares the transit again with `public=True` (`route_declare` of the core; limited by
  `BAZIS_THROTTLE_PUBLIC` per user or IP address, or by
  `route_declare(..., public=True, dependencies=[throttle(...)])`); the transit permissions
  of the roles for anonymous users (`Role(for_anonymous=True)`, selector `all`) still
  decide which transits they make, and the transit has no author:

  ```python
  from bazis.core.routes_abstract.initial import route_declare

  class RequestGuestRouteSet(StatusyRouteSetBase):
      model = apps.get_model('service.Request')
      actions = ['action_transit']

      @classmethod
      def get_url_prefix(cls) -> str:
          return '/service/request_guest'

      action_transit = route_declare(StatusyRouteSetBase.action_transit, public=True)
  ```

  Declare `default_route = True` on the main route of the model (a second route set of a
  model, see the guide of the core).
- Meta: `state_actions` (retrieve: allowed transits, their body and `restricts` = the
  validator errors), `for_transit` (list, bazis-statusy 2.13: the transits the user may make
  on each object of the page, `{"<pk>": ["<transit id>", ...]}`, the ids sorted, an object
  without one left out; `allow_transits` of the object, what the transit endpoint of the
  route set accepts: the transit permissions by selector and status from the status of the
  object; the validators are not called: a transit it lists may still be refused with 422;
  one query per condition of the permissions, not per object; a board shows the transits
  of a card by it). Both list exactly what `POST /{item_id}/transit/` of the route set
  takes: on a route set whose `action_transit` is not public, an anonymous user gets no
  transit in `state_actions` nor in `for_transit` (bazis-statusy 2.13); on a route set that
  declares it `public=True`, those of the roles for anonymous users. `for_transit` lists
  the transits of the top level of `state_actions` (bazis-statusy 2.14): the child
  transits of a `TransitRelation` are left out, `state_actions` shows them only nested
  under their parent.
- Meta `status_aggs` (list: the counts by status of the visible objects with the filter of
  the request without `status` and the search, applied by the services of the route as the
  list does, so restricted to what the route shows) and `status_allowed` (list).

## Transits in code and the history

- `item.get_transit('<transit id>')` is the transit of the model with that id that starts
  from the current status of the item, else None (check it); `item.instance_transits`
  are all of them. Take the transit of `transit_apply` with it.
- `item.transit_apply(transit, user, payload=None)` makes only a transit of the model of
  the item (its content type) that starts from the current status of the item, a transit
  `get_transit` gives: another one fails with 400 `ERR_TRANSIT`
  (`JsonApiBazisException`) before its validators, nothing written.
  `payload` is the dict of the body of the transit endpoint (`{'dt_closed': '2026-...'}`)
  or an instance of a payload model (`ClosePayload(dt_closed=...)`, bazis-statusy 2.12),
  validated as its data with the payload type of the transit: a transit whose methods
  annotate several payload models takes the fields of all of them, so pass the dict, or
  an instance of `Model.get_transit_payload_type(transit)`; missing fields are 422
  (`JsonApiBazisException`), as on the endpoint. The methods receive the instance of the
  payload type, not the object passed. It runs the
  validators (with `user`), writes the history record, runs the actions before, sets
  `status`, `status_dt`, `status_author`, runs the actions after and returns the item
  read again. It checks
  neither the permissions of `user` nor `is_schema_validate` (the transit endpoint does).
- The actor: `user` is the `author` of the history record and the `status_author`. A
  transit the system makes (an automatic confirmation, a task) passes `None`: the record
  has no author. Do not pass the user of the request for it: the history would say that
  he made a transit his permissions may not allow. A project that names its system actor
  passes a user of its own for it.
- An automatic transit on create, in `hook_after_create` of the route, after `super()`:
  bazis-permit checks the item against the `item.add` permissions of the user there, with
  the status of creation, so the transit (the server's, not the user's) comes after the
  check and the role needs `item.add` of the initial status only. By itself the
  transit is validated with the create, once, as `create` with the user of the route
  (`changes.user`, also for a transit without a user), but its validators run before that
  validation. Validate the new item first, so that an invalid one answers with the errors
  of its fields (422 `ERR_ITEM_INVALID`), not with the error of the transit
  (`ERR_TRANSIT`); then the item is validated twice, `('create', user)` before the
  transit and `('transit', user)` after it (keep `validate_item` cheap or check
  `changes.source`):

  ```python
  from bazis.core.item_validation import defer_validate_item

  class BookingRouteSet(StatusyRouteSetBase):
      def hook_after_create(self, item):
          super().hook_after_create(item)
          if not item.room.requires_approval:
              with defer_validate_item() as scope:
                  scope.validate()
              # None if the transit does not start from the status of the new item
              if transit := item.get_transit('confirm'):
                  item.transit_apply(transit, None)
  ```

- The payload of a transit is kept in its history record (bazis-statusy 2.15): the
  validated payload (`model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True)` of the payload type), under
  `extra['payload']`; a transit without a payload type, or a record made before 2.15,
  has none. **Whoever has the `history` permission reads the payload** (the route below):
  keep no secret in it, or mark the field `NOT_IN_HISTORY`
  (`from bazis.contrib.statusy.schemas import NOT_IN_HISTORY`; in the payload model
  `secret: Annotated[str | None, NOT_IN_HISTORY] = None`, or the mark on a member of its
  `Optional`, `Annotated[str, NOT_IN_HISTORY] | None`): it is validated and the methods of
  the transit receive it, from a dict (the endpoint) or a payload model instance
  (`transit_apply`), but the record does not keep the field. The mark goes on a field of
  the payload model only: one elsewhere (an item of a list or a dict, a field of a nested
  model) is `ImproperlyConfigured` when the payload type is built (the transit, its
  `state_actions`, the contract export), naming the field. No migration: `extra` is the
  field of the record.
- The history: `item.statusy_transits` (the model `<Model>StatusyTransit` of the app), one
  record per transit with `transit`, `status` (the new one), `dt`, `author` and `extra`
  (JSON, since 2.15 `{"status_src": "<the status it started from>", "payload": {...}}`,
  `payload` only for a transit with a payload type; an action may add keys of its own, not
  touch these; `{}` for a record made before 2.15); order it by `dt`. `StatusyAdminMixin` shows it in the admin. A status
  written without a transit (`QuerySet.update(status=...)` in test data) has no record.

### The history in the API: `status_history`

The history model is not a JSON:API resource. `GET /{item_id}/status_history/` of
`StatusyRouteSetBase` (bazis-statusy 2.15) returns it with the names and the payload, a
plain JSON document, not a JSON:API one:

```json
{"data": [{"transit": {"id": "to_paid", "name": "Pay"}, "status_src": "draft",
           "status_dst": "paid", "dt": "2026-03-01T10:00:00Z",
           "author": {"id": "<user id>", "type": "users.user"}, "payload": {"dt_closed": "..."}}]}
```

The oldest first; `author` is null for a transit of the system, `payload` null for a
transit without one; `status_src` is the status the transit started from, kept in the
record (for a record made before 2.15, the source status of the current definition of the
transit). It needs the permission `item.history` of the item (selector and status, as the other
item permissions); an item the user cannot view is 404 first, as at its retrieve, a user
without `history` is 403. The permission is its own, not `view`, because of the payloads
(and the names of the transits): what the users sent with the transits, which `view` of
the item does not show. Grant it only to the roles that may read them. The calculated
field `status_history` (below) is the compact form, read with the item in one subquery
under `view`; the route is the full, canonical form. A route set that should not give it lists its
`actions` without `action_status_history`.

`StatusyMixin` also has the calculated field `status_history` (bazis-statusy 2.12): the transits of the item, the
oldest first, each `{"transit": "<transit id>", "status": "<status id>", "dt": "<ISO
time>", "author": "<user id>" | null}` (null for a transit of the system). A route shows it
with `include` (fetched in the query of the route, one subquery, for a list too):

```python
class OrderRouteSet(StatusyRouteSetBase):
    model = apps.get_model('shop.Order')
    fields = {None: SchemaFields(include={'status_history': None})}
```

It is a read-only field of the item: whoever views the item reads its history (the
`view` permissions by status and selector), nobody else; a field permission hides it
(`shop.order.field.view.all.all.status_history.disable`). A client names the transits
and statuses by their ids (the read-only routes `statusy/transit/` and `statusy/status/`
under the prefix of the API router, registered with `bazis.contrib.statusy.router`) and the authors by the users it may read. A history with
other data (the `extra` of the records, the names of the authors) is a `calc_property` of
the model of its own over `statusy_transits` (see the guide of the core).

## Rules

- The status changes only through `POST /{item_id}/transit/`: the UPDATE schema of
  `StatusyRouteSetBase` has no `status`, `status_dt`, `status_author`, the CREATE schema no
  `status_dt`, `status_author` (a write with them is 422 `ERR_VALIDATE` `extra_forbidden`
  from bazis 2.12, at `/data/relationships/<f>` or `/data/attributes/status_dt`; before it
  they were ignored); the `fields` of a route add up with them, do not exclude them again.
  The CREATE schema accepts an initial `status` (the initial status if omitted): the
  `add` permissions by status restrict it (`item.add.all.draft`: only `draft`; checked on
  the created item by bazis-permit 2.11, see Setup), or exclude it
  (`CrudApiAction.CREATE: SchemaFields(exclude={'status': None})`: always the initial
  status).
  `StatusyRouteSetBase` adds the actions `action_transit` and `action_schema_transit` and
  no hooks (those of bazis-permit apply).
- Every JSON:API route that changes a statusy model inherits `StatusyRouteSetBase` (`statusy.W001`);
  the routes of `StatusyChildMixin` models inherit `StatusySimpleRouteSetBase`. A read-only
  route of the model (a projection that lists its `actions` without the create, update and
  relationships actions) needs neither and is not reported; it does not apply the
  permissions by status either: it is a route without permissions (see "another route of
  a protected model" in the guide of bazis-permit, `permit.W002`), its `get_queryset`
  decides what it shows. To keep the permissions by status on a read-only route, inherit
  `StatusyRouteSetBase` and list its `actions`; a plain `PermitRouteBase` does not apply the
  status segment of the permissions (only `PermitStatusyHandler` does).
- Validators are also called with `payload is payload_validate_none` (to build
  `state_actions`): check it before reading the payload.
- Decorated methods are defined directly in a model class (or its mixin); `Transit` lists
  their method names. A transit runs in a transaction.
- A child object whose status is the parent's: `StatusyChildMixin` with the
  classmethod `get_status_field()` returning the path to the status of the parent; list
  its route in `routes_child` of the parent route to validate the children with it on a
  transit (else the default route of the child model):

  ```python
  class OrderItem(StatusyChildMixin, DtMixin, UuidMixin, JsonApiMixin):
      order = models.ForeignKey(Order, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='items')

      @classmethod                 # a classmethod: read on the class when the models load
      def get_status_field(cls):
          return 'order__status_id'

  class OrderItemRouteSet(StatusySimpleRouteSetBase):
      model = apps.get_model('shop.OrderItem')
  ```
 `StatusyChildMixin` is a
  `PermitModelMixin` (as `StatusyMixin`): its objects are restricted by the permissions
  of the user, with selectors (`author`) and the status of the parent
  (`entity.order_item.item.view.author.draft`), on its route and through the relations
  (`included`, filters) of the other routes.
- A transit of the parent with `is_schema_validate` validates the parent with its transit
  schema and every child (all of them, also those the user does not view) with the
  transit schema of its route, read as that route reads its objects (with the
  `calc_property` fields of the schema, since 2.12.0): the fields with the restrictions of the field permissions
  of the user for the transits of the child model
  (`shop.order_item.field.transit.all.all.price.notnull`), a failure is 422: the errors of
  the fields of a child the user views (`source` with its `id`, `type` and `pointer`);
  for the children he does not view one error that names none of them,
  `ERR_TRANSIT_CHILDREN_INVALID` `Some related items are not valid for this transit`
  (only when no child he views is invalid). The permission of the transit is the one of the parent
  (`shop.order.item.transit.author.draft.submit`): grant no `transit` item permission of
  the child models for it (since 2.10.0; before it the transit was 403 without them). Such
  a permission only opens `GET /{item_id}/schema_transit/` of the child route.
- A transit validates the item once with `JsonApiMixin.validate_item` (bazis 2.10.0):
  `changes.source == 'transit'`, `changes.fields` with `status`, `status_dt`,
  `status_author` and the fields the actions set, `changes.user` the user of the transit;
  a failure rolls the transit back (422 `ERR_ITEM_INVALID` on the transit endpoint). The
  source and the user come from the outermost block: a transit inside a write of a route
  (`hook_after_create`) is validated with that write, once, as `create` with the user of
  the route. Keep the invariants of the item there (a validator of a transit checks only
  that transit).
- `item.transit_apply(transit, user, payload)` in code validates but does not check
  permissions (the payload: see Transits in code); `@transit_link` returns it bound to the
  transit whose `source_link` is the method.

## Statuses and transits as data

Without `workflow.py` (or besides it, for what the admin changes), the statuses and
transits are rows:

- Statuses and transitions are data (`bazis.contrib.statusy.models`): create `Status`
  (string `id`) and `Transit` (`id`, `model` =
  `StatusyContentType.objects.get_for_model(Order)`, `status_src`, `status_dst`, lists of
  method names `validators`, `actions_before`, `actions_after`) in code or in the admin
  (Statusy > Status models: the transitions inline offers the decorated methods). Their
  names are the columns `name_en` and `name_ru` (as the roles of bazis-permit), whatever
  the languages of the project: a data migration sets both.
- `StatusyContentType` is a proxy of the `ContentType` of Django limited to the statusy
  models (its manager caches them: `StatusyContentType.objects.clear_cache()` in a test that
  creates the transits). A data migration has no proxy managers and runs before the content
  types are created: take the content type itself and set `model_id`:

  ```python
  def create_workflow(apps, schema_editor):
      content_type = apps.get_model('contenttypes', 'ContentType').objects.get_or_create(
          app_label='shop', model='order'
      )[0]
      status = apps.get_model('statusy', 'Status').objects
      draft = status.update_or_create(id='draft', defaults={'name_en': 'Draft', 'name_ru': 'Черновик'})[0]
      paid = status.update_or_create(id='paid', defaults={'name_en': 'Paid', 'name_ru': 'Оплачен'})[0]
      apps.get_model('statusy', 'Transit').objects.update_or_create(
          id='to_paid',
          defaults={
              'name_en': 'Pay', 'name_ru': 'Оплатить', 'model_id': content_type.pk,
              'status_src': draft, 'status_dst': paid,
              'validators': ['validator_paid'], 'actions_before': ['before_date'],
          },
      )
  ```

  Depend on `('contenttypes', '0002_remove_content_type_name')`, the latest migration of
  `statusy` and of the app of the model.

pitfalls.text: tasks run only while `manage.py bg_scheduler` runs (from the directory of manage.py)
BgRoute.restrict_queryset is also what the other routes link and include: a custom task route changes the rule there
a task runs without the request, its user or its language: pass the user id and the language as arguments, author=user
the file of a task is downloaded from GET /api/v1/bg/task/{id}/download/: its file attribute is a public media URL
the task route, and `included` of any route, gives authors `Error` for an error and no log (fields `error` and `log` of BgRoute); a custom task route subclasses BgRoute to keep them
do not declare permit_public = True on the task routes: they restrict the tasks themselves
with is_transaction, next_phase, progress syncs and set_result commit the work done so far
the scheduler deletes waiting tasks whose class path no longer imports

declare a periodic task in <app>/schedules.py, not with get_or_create in a data migration
