agents_md:
# bazis-bg — guide for AI agents

Background tasks stored in PostgreSQL (no broker): a task class is queued with `delay()`
as a `Task` row, the `bg_scheduler` process starts handler processes that run the tasks,
schedules periodic tasks (`TaskCron`) and enforces the limits of each class. Also bases for
xlsx exports and imports. Needs bazis-author (tasks have an `author`).

### The sections

Read a section with `package_guide("bazis-bg", "<section>")` when the step at hand needs
it; `guide_search` finds the part of a section that answers a question. A product with
background work needs Setup, Tasks and Rules.

| Section | Read it when |
|---|---|
| Setup | you install it: the app, where the task classes live, `bg_scheduler` and the handlers, `bg_task`, the storage of the files of the tasks |
| Tasks | you write a task: `BgBase`, `delay()`, the names and phases (lazy texts), the states, the hooks, the transactions |
| Following a task from a client | an action of a route starts a task and the client follows it: `task_accepted`, the fields of the task route, the progress of the phases, the error |
| Exports and imports | a task writes or reads xlsx: `BgBaseDownloadModel`, `BgBaseDownload`, `BgBaseLoad`, an export for the user of a request, the admin actions |
| Periodic tasks and cleanup | a task runs on a schedule: `Schedule` in `schedules.py`, what `migrate` applies, a periodic task of an old data migration, the checks `bg.*`, the cleanup |
| Rules | before you write the code, once: who sees the tasks, the download of their files, the class paths, the handlers |

## Setup

- `BS_INSTALLED_APPS` includes `bazis.contrib.bg`; `python manage.py migrate`.
- Put the task classes in `<app>/bg/*.py`: every module of the `bg` package of an installed
  app is imported at startup.
- Run one `python manage.py bg_scheduler` in the directory of `manage.py`: it starts
  `manage.py bg_handler --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>` processes to keep
  `BAZIS_TASK_HANDLERS_LOCAL` (5) registered handlers, on free ports from
  `BAZIS_TASK_HANDLER_PORT` (49100), and serves `/healthcheck` on
  `BAZIS_TASK_SCHEDULER_PORT` (49001). A handler runs one task at a time and exits after
  2–4 hours (the scheduler starts another). Without the scheduler, tasks stay `waiting`.
- `python manage.py bg_task --task_id <id>` runs one task in the current process (tests,
  debugging).
- Files of tasks: `BS_BAZIS_STORAGE_BG` (import path of a storage class; default the file
  system storage in `MEDIA_ROOT`), in the folder `BAZIS_TASK_FOLDER` (`bg`), stored as
  `<token>_<name>` with a random token (the media host serves them without a check, the
  token keeps their names from being guessed). Clients download them from
  `GET /api/v1/bg/task/{id}/download/` (see Rules).

## Tasks

```python
from bazis.contrib.bg.basic.base import BgBase

class Recalc(BgBase):
    name = 'Recalculate prices'     # required (the admin lists only named classes)
    parallel = 1                    # at most N running tasks of this class
    blocked = ['shop.bg.tasks.Import']   # wait while these classes (module.Class) run

    def __init__(self, category_id):    # the args/kwargs of delay()
        self.category_id = category_id

    def handle(self):
        qs = Product.objects.filter(category_id=self.category_id)
        self.next_phase('Prices', expected=qs.count())
        for product in qs:
            ...
            self.progress()          # saved to the task every 3 s; checks the interruption
        self.set_result({'count': qs.count()})

task = Recalc.delay(category_id, author=user)   # -> Task (state `waiting`)
```

- `delay()` arguments are stored as JSON. Reserved keyword arguments: `name`, `fp` (a file
  saved to `task.file`), `author`, `envs` (stored, not applied).
- The name of a task class, the `name=` of `delay()` and the names of the phases
  (`next_phase`) may be lazy texts (`gettext_lazy`, English msgids). The class keeps the
  lazy name (the admin lists it in the language of its request); a task stores text in the
  language active when it is written: `Task.name` at `delay()` (the language of the
  request in a route; the scheduler queues a periodic task in `LANGUAGE_CODE`), a phase
  (`phase` and its record in `phases_history`) at `next_phase` in the handler process, in
  `LANGUAGE_CODE` unless the task activates a language (`translation.override(self.language)`
  in `handle`, as the export below). A client shows the stored text as it is.
- States: `waiting` → `starting` → `running` → `done`; `task.is_success`, `is_error`
  (`error` holds the traceback; the task route gives the author `Error` only, see
  Rules), `is_interrupt`; `phase`, `log`, `result`, `file`.
- Hooks: `pre_handle`, `post_handle`, `excepting` (error), `interrupting`, `finishing`
  (always). The admin "Interrupt" button sets `interrupt`; the task stops at its next
  `progress` sync, `next_phase`, `flush` or `set_result`.
- `is_transaction = True` (default) runs the task with autocommit off, but every
  `next_phase`, `flush`, `set_result` (and synced `progress`) commits the work done so far;
  an error rolls back only since the last commit.

## Following a task from a client

An action of a route that starts work queues the task with `author=user` (or the user does
not see it) and answers `task_accepted(task)` (`bazis.contrib.bg.routes`): 202 with
`{"data": {"type": "bg.task", "id": "<id>"}}` and `Location: /api/v1/bg/task/<id>/`, the
URL of the task in the default route of the tasks. The client (the task progress component
of bazis-front) polls that URL until `state` is `done`:

```python
from bazis.contrib.bg.routes import task_accepted

class ReportRouteSet(UserRequiredRouteBase):
    @http_post('/calc/', status_code=202, kind=RouteKind.OTHER)
    def action_calc(self, **kwargs):
        return task_accepted(CalcData.delay(author=self.inject.user))
```

- `state`: `waiting`, `starting`, `running`, `done`. Done, the task succeeded when `error`
  is empty and `interrupt` false; `phase` is then `completed`, `error`, `interrupted` or a
  text of the handler when the process of the task failed.
- `expected` and `performed` are those of the current `phase` (a number or a dict of
  numbers, as the task gives them; `performed` from the first sync of `progress`, every 3 s,
  or `flush`). A phase that ends is moved to `phases_history` as `{phase, duration,
  expected, performed}` and both are set to null: a progress bar reads them while `running`
  and the finished phases from `phases_history`; once the task is done both are null.
- `error`: `Error` for the author of a failed task (null or empty otherwise), the traceback
  for staff; `log` is null for the author. A client that must show the cause to the author
  reads it from a field of the product (the task writes it with `set_result`, a message
  it chooses), not from the traceback.
- `result` is what the task gave `set_result`; its file is downloaded from
  `/api/v1/bg/task/{id}/download/`, not from the `file` attribute (see Rules).

## Exports and imports

- Exports: `BgBaseDownloadModel` (`model`, `fields_read`; all objects, override
  `get_queryset`) or `BgBaseDownload` (`fields_read`, `get_queryset`, `get_count`,
  `get_titles`, `file_name`) write xlsx to `task.file` (a zip above `limit_rows_split`
  rows). Imports: `BgBaseLoad` reads the `.xlsx` (or `.zip` of them) given as `delay(fp=...)` and passes
  the rows as dicts keyed by `fields_read` to `load(reader)`; `skip_titles = True` skips
  the header row.
- An export for the user of a request (an action of a route): the task runs in the
  handler process, without the request, its user or its language. Queue it with JSON
  arguments (ids, ISO dates) and `author=user`, so that the user reads the task at
  `/api/v1/bg/task/{id}/` and downloads its file from `/api/v1/bg/task/{id}/download/`;
  restrict the rows with the `restrict_queryset` of the default route of the model for
  that user; write the texts in the language of the request:

  ```python
  # the route: @http_post('/export/', status_code=202, kind=RouteKind.OTHER) def action_export(self, ...)
  task = OrdersExport.delay(user_id=str(user.pk), language=get_language(), author=user)
  # ... return task_accepted(task)    (see Following a task from a client)

  class OrdersExport(BgBaseDownload):
      name = 'Orders'
      fields_read = ['number', 'title']
      file_name = 'orders'

      def __init__(self, user_id, language):
          self.user = get_user_model().objects.get(pk=user_id)
          self.language = language

      def handle(self):
          with translation.override(self.language):
              super().handle()

      def get_titles(self):           # column titles (lazy texts are written translated)
          return {'number': _('Number'), 'title': _('Title')}

      def queryset(self):
          qs = OrderRouteSet.restrict_queryset(Order.objects.all(), CrudAccessAction.VIEW,
                                               user=self.user)
          return qs.order_by('number')

      def get_count(self):            # required: the expected number of rows
          return self.queryset().count()

      def get_queryset(self):         # objects or dicts keyed by fields_read
          return self.queryset()
  ```
- Admin: `LoadDownloadAdminMixin` with `tasks_download`, `tasks_load`, `tasks_handler`
  (task classes, in the admin class body) adds actions that start them without arguments
  (`tasks_load` with the uploaded file). Its change list is `admin/bg/load_download_change_list.html`:
  an admin class with a `change_list_template` of its own extends that template.

## Periodic tasks and cleanup

A periodic task of a product is declared in the `schedules.py` module of an application,
not in the admin nor in a data migration:

```python
# training/schedules.py
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from bazis.contrib.bg.declare import Schedule

SCHEDULES = [
    Schedule('deadlines_remind', 'training.bg.deadlines.RemindDeadlines', '0 6 * * *',
             _('Deadline reminders'), kwargs={'days': 3}),
    Schedule('stats_refresh', StatsRefresh, 3600),      # the class, or its path
]
```

- `Schedule(slug, task, period, name=None, kwargs={}, enabled=True)`: `task` is a `BgBase`
  class with a `name` (or its path `module.Class`); `period` is seconds after the previous
  run finished (`3600`, `"3600"`) or a cron expression in UTC (`"0 3 * * *"`); `name` an
  English msgid stored in `LANGUAGE_CODE` (the name of the task class without it);
  `kwargs` the JSON keyword arguments of the task (not `name`, `fp`, `author`, `envs`).
  `TaskCron.name` is one column: the declared name is stored translated into
  `LANGUAGE_CODE` (a new `LANGUAGE_CODE` renames it at the next `migrate`).
- `migrate` applies them (`post_migrate`, also sent by `flush`) once all the migrations of
  the project are applied, in one transaction: the periodic task (`TaskCron`) of each slug
  is created or updated as declared and marked `managed`; a new period or `enabled`
  resets its next run time. Applied again it writes nothing. A periodic task of the slug
  that exists unmarked (made in the admin) is taken over with a warning in the log. A
  managed one no longer declared is disabled and unmarked: an ordinary periodic task the
  admin may enable again, not deleted (its tasks reference it). This differs from the
  roles of bazis-permit and the transits of bazis-statusy, which stay managed with a
  warning: a periodic task left enabled would keep running. Periodic tasks made in the
  admin are left as they are.
- A data migration with `TaskCron.objects.get_or_create(...)` is the wrong tool: it runs
  once, so a new period in the code never reaches a database that has the row, and it
  depends on the migrations of the package.
- Moving a periodic task made by such a migration (or in the admin) to `schedules.py`: its
  row has no slug, so the schedule creates a second enabled one and the task runs twice
  (`bg.W002` reports it). Delete the old row and let the declaration own the schedule: in
  the admin, or with a data migration of the product (keep the old migration; this works
  whether `migrate` has already created the declared row or not, as that one has a slug):

  ```python
  def delete_old_cron(apps, schema_editor):
      apps.get_model('bg', 'TaskCron').objects.filter(
          cls_path='training.bg.deadlines.RemindDeadlines', slug=None,
      ).delete()

  # depends on the old get_or_create migration and on ('bg', '0006_taskcron_slug_managed')
  operations = [migrations.RunPython(delete_old_cron, migrations.RunPython.noop)]
  ```

  Add `kwargs={...}` to the filter if other periodic tasks of the admin run the same class.
  The tasks the old row started are kept but no longer linked to a periodic task
  (`on_delete=SET_NULL`): the cleanup counts them as manual tasks (`BAZIS_TASK_LIFETIME`).
- The admin shows a declared periodic task read-only besides `dt_run` (setting it runs the
  task at that time) and `envs`, and does not delete it.
- Checks: `bg.E001` (the slug, a duplicate, the name, the period, the kwargs, `enabled`),
  `bg.E002` (the task class does not import, is not a named `BgBase`, or the kwargs do not
  fit its `__init__`); with a database (`bazis_doctor`) `bg.W001` (the database differs
  from the declarations: run `migrate`) and `bg.W002` (an enabled periodic task that is
  not managed runs the task of a schedule with its kwargs: delete it).
- Tests: the migrated test database has them; `bazis_test_utils` (`apply_declarations()`,
  the fixture `bazis_declared`) applies them again for a test that changes them.
- `bazis.contrib.bg.declare.apply_declarations(using, schedules=None, dry_run=False)`
  returns the changes; `dry_run` only lists them; `schedules` are `(module, Schedule)`
  pairs, as `declarations()` gives them.
- The cleanup is the periodic task `bg_tasks_clean` that bazis-bg declares itself
  (`bazis/contrib/bg/schedules.py`): it deletes the tasks (and their files) not updated for
  `BAZIS_TASK_LIFETIME` (manual, 90 days) or `BAZIS_TASK_CRON_LIFETIME` (periodic, 6 hours)
  seconds, dynamic settings (edited in the admin) read when it runs. It runs every
  `BAZIS_TASK_CRON_CLEANUP` (3600) seconds unless `BAZIS_TASK_CLEANUP` is false: these two
  are environment settings applied by `migrate`. A product does not declare it again.
  It deletes the tasks through the ORM, by portions of 1000 in a transaction each, so the
  `on_delete` of a foreign key to `bg.Task` applies (`SET_NULL` unlinks, `CASCADE`
  deletes), and the files of a portion once its rows are committed (a file the storage
  fails to delete is logged and left). A task kept by `PROTECT` or `RESTRICT` is logged and left with its
  file; the portion that holds it is deleted task by task at every run, so prefer
  `SET_NULL` for a reference that may outlive the task.
  `manage.py cleanup_init` is deprecated and does nothing (removed in 2.7).

## Rules

- The task route of `bazis.contrib.bg.router` requires authentication and shows a user only
  the tasks whose `author` he is (staff see all): tasks hold arguments, logs and files.
  The author is set by `delay(author=user)` or, inside the API routes, from the current
  user; tasks queued elsewhere (admin, scheduler, scripts) have no author and only staff
  see them. Keep custom task routes as restrictive.
- The rule is the classmethod `BgRoute.restrict_queryset` (none for an anonymous user; the
  authenticated user of the request `UserMixin.CTX_USER_REQUEST` when the caller passes
  no user): as the default route of `bg.Task` it is also what the other routes link and
  include (the core, Bazis 2.7). `CTX_USER_REQUEST` is set by the routes of bazis-users
  (`UserRouteBase`) and its Django middleware: on a route without a user (a plain
  `JsonapiRouteBase`) a logged-in user is anonymous for the tasks (403 for his own task,
  left out of `included`). A model with a foreign key to `bg.Task` (the sample
  `entity.Report`) links only the tasks the user sees (403 `ERR_RELATION_ACCESS`
  otherwise) and `include` leaves out the others; its route set needs no checks of its
  own. A custom task route of `bg.Task` changes the rule in `restrict_queryset` and
  declares `default_route = True`.
- The traceback of an error and the log hold paths, code and data of the server: the task
  route gives a user who is not staff `Error` for an error (an error that is null or empty
  stays so; no part of the text: a message may quote anything, even a traceback, so the
  class read from it is not safe either) and no log; staff read both. The rule is the
  source of the fields `error` and `log` in `BgRoute.fields` (`error_shown`, `log_shown`: the
  user of the request, `UserMixin.authenticated_user(None)`), so `included` of any route
  gives the same `Error` and null, and they are no key of a filter or a sorting for anyone,
  also through a relation of another route (staff read the traceback in the admin). A
  custom task route subclasses `BgRoute` to keep this.
- `GET /api/v1/bg/task/{id}/download/` serves the file of a task the user sees (401 for an
  anonymous user, 404 for another user's task, a task without a file or a file missing from
  the storage) as a download named after the file without its token, with `nosniff`,
  `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Link the
  file to this route, not to the `file` attribute: that is the URL of the media host,
  which serves it to anyone who has the link. A custom task route that lists its
  `actions` adds `action_download`.
- `BgRoute` and its subclasses restrict the tasks with their own `restrict_queryset`:
  `permit.W002` of bazis-permit does not apply to them from bazis-permit 2.10 (do not
  declare `permit_public = True`, which says the data is public). With bazis-permit 2.9
  the warning is a false positive.
- A task class is found by its path (`module.Class`): the scheduler deletes waiting tasks
  whose class does not import, so keep the path when tasks may be queued.
- A task with the same arguments as a running task of its class waits for it.
- A handler runs many tasks in one process: release what a task attaches to global state
  (loggers, settings, connections).

agents_md:
# bazis-async-background — guide for AI agents

Background tasks over Kafka (FastStream) for Bazis. An endpoint queues a task with
`enqueue_task_async` and returns its id; consumer processes run the task; the statuses are
stored in Redis and pushed to the WebSocket channel of the client (bazis-ws); the client
reads the result at `GET <router prefix>/async_background_response/{task_id}/`
(`/api/v1/...` with `BazisRouter(prefix='/api/v1')`).

## Setup

```bash
BS_INSTALLED_APPS='["bazis.contrib.async_background", ...]'
BS_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=kafka1:9092,kafka2:9092
BS_KAFKA_TOPIC_ASYNC_BG=myproject_async_background
BS_KAFKA_GROUP_ID=myproject
BS_KAFKA_TASKS='["myapp.tasks"]'        # modules the consumer imports
```

- Services: Kafka, and Redis as `BS_CACHES__DEFAULT__LOCATION` (statuses and pub/sub).
- If `BS_BAZIS_APPS` (or `BS_BAZIS_CONFIG_APPS`) is set, list
  `bazis.contrib.async_background` there, or its `KAFKA_*` settings do not exist.
- Register the result route: `router.register('bazis.contrib.async_background.router')`.
- Run consumers with the same settings as the API, from the directory of `manage.py`:
  `python manage.py kafka_consumer_single` (one process, e.g. per pod) or
  `python manage.py kafka_consumer_multiple --consumers-count=N` (default 15;
  `--restart-delay-sec` default 1.0, `--max-restarts` default unlimited). Without
  `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` and `KAFKA_TOPIC_ASYNC_BG` the consumer exits with an error.
  With `KAFKA_CONSUMER_LIFETIME_SEC` (+ `_JITTER_SEC`) a consumer exits after its lifetime;
  `kafka_consumer_multiple` starts a new one.

## Queue a task

```python
from django.conf import settings
from fastapi import Request
from bazis.contrib.async_background.producer import enqueue_task_async
from bazis.contrib.async_background.utils import ChannelNameError, resolve_channel_name_async
from bazis.core.errors import JsonApi401Exception

@router.post('/report/', status_code=202)
async def report(request: Request, payload: ReportPayload) -> dict:   # pydantic model
    try:
        channel_name = await resolve_channel_name_async(request)
    except ChannelNameError as err:
        raise JsonApi401Exception from err
    task = await enqueue_task_async(topic_name=settings.KAFKA_TOPIC_ASYNC_BG,
                                    channel_name=channel_name, payload=payload)
    return {'data': None, 'meta': {'task_id': task.task_id}}
```

`resolve_channel_name_async` reads `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: a session JWT gives the
user channel, any other token the anonymous channel of bazis-ws. Tasks with the same
`partition_marker` (the Kafka key) go to the same partition.

## Run a task (a module listed in `KAFKA_TASKS`)

```python
from django.conf import settings
from bazis.contrib.async_background.broker import get_broker_for_consumer, subscriber_kwargs
from bazis.contrib.async_background.schemas import KafkaTask, TaskStatus
from bazis.contrib.async_background.utils import set_and_publish_status_async

@get_broker_for_consumer().subscriber(settings.KAFKA_TOPIC_ASYNC_BG, **subscriber_kwargs())
async def run_report(task: KafkaTask[ReportPayload]):
    await set_and_publish_status_async(task_id=task.task_id, channel_name=task.channel_name,
                                       status=TaskStatus.PROCESSING)
    ...
    await set_and_publish_status_async(task_id=task.task_id, channel_name=task.channel_name,
                                       status=TaskStatus.COMPLETED, response={...})
```

## Results

- Statuses: `pending` (set before publishing), `processing`, `completed`, `failed`.
  Stored under `async_bg:task:<task_id>` for `KAFKA_RESPONSE_HOLD_SEC` (default 86400).
- The WS channel receives `{"status", "task_id", "action": "async_bg"}`, not the result.
- `GET /async_background_response/{task_id}/` needs the same token as the request that
  queued the task: no or invalid token 401, another channel 403, unknown task 404. It returns
  `response`, or `{"status": "not ready"}`; `?full_response=true` returns the stored status.

## Rules

- Set `KAFKA_GROUP_ID`: without a consumer group offsets are not committed and every
  consumer receives every task.
- Get the channel only from `resolve_channel_name_async`: it owns the results.
- A task sets its final status itself: on an exception, set `TaskStatus.FAILED` with a
  generic error, or the task stays `processing`. Do not store exception texts.
- Always pass `**subscriber_kwargs()` to `subscriber(...)`. With the default
  `KAFKA_ACK_POLICY=ack` a failed message is not redelivered; `nack_on_error` redelivers it
  and blocks its partition. `KAFKA_ENABLE_AUTO_COMMIT=true` can lose messages.

## Tests

`bazis.contrib.async_background.testing` (pytest): import its
`pytest_collection_modifyitems` into the conftest to skip the tests marked
`run_with_consumer` without Kafka settings; `wait_for_task(task_id)` returns the stored
status once a consumer has completed the task, `wait_for_tasks()` waits until none is
pending or processing, `redis_client()` and `delete_tasks()` read and delete the stored
statuses. A consumer shares the database of the tests: migrate it and run pytest with
`--reuse-db`.

agents_md:
# bazis-async-request — guide for AI agents

Runs any HTTP request of a Bazis API in the background: a request with the header
`X-Async-Background` is queued in Kafka (bazis-async-background) and answered 202; a
consumer replays it through the ASGI application and stores the response for
`GET /async_background_response/{task_id}/`. Use it for slow endpoints and bulk changes.

## Setup

```bash
BS_INSTALLED_APPS='[..., "bazis.contrib.async_request", "bazis.contrib.async_background"]'
BS_KAFKA_TASKS='["bazis.contrib.async_request.tasks"]'   # the consumer of the requests
BS_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=kafka:9092
BS_KAFKA_TOPIC_ASYNC_BG=myproject_async_request
BS_KAFKA_GROUP_ID=myproject
```

```python
# the main module of the application (as sample/sample/main.py)
from bazis.contrib.async_request.middleware import AsyncRequestMiddleware
from bazis.core.app import app

app.add_middleware(AsyncRequestMiddleware)      # not added automatically

# the root router
router.register('bazis.contrib.async_background.router')    # async_request.E001
```

- Services and consumers as in bazis-async-background: Kafka, Redis, and
  `python manage.py kafka_consumer_single` (or `kafka_consumer_multiple`) with the same
  settings and database as the API.
- Without Kafka settings the middleware executes these requests synchronously and only
  logs a warning (`async_request.W001`).

## Client

- Send the request as usual plus `X-Async-Background: true` (the header's presence is
  enough) and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: a session JWT, or an anonymous token of
  bazis-ws (16–128 characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`). Without a valid token: 401. The request
  is replayed with the same header: routes that read the user (bazis-users, permit, author)
  answer 401 to an anonymous token, so use it only for routes that do not.
- Answer: 202 `{"data": null, "meta": {"async_request_id": <id>}}` (the task id).
  Status updates arrive on the WebSocket channel of the token.
- Result: `GET .../async_background_response/{task_id}/` with the same token returns
  `{"task_id", "endpoint", "status", "headers", "response"}` of the replayed request
  (an HTTP error is a `completed` task with its status); `{"status": "not ready"}` before.

## Endpoints only for background requests

```python
from fastapi import Depends
from bazis.contrib.async_request.utils import require_async

@router.post('/reports/generate/', dependencies=[Depends(require_async)])
async def generate_report(...): ...

class ShopRouteSet(JsonapiRouteBase):
    @inject_make(CrudApiAction.UPDATE)          # bazis.core.routes_abstract.initial
    class InjectRequireAsync:
        async_request: None = Depends(require_async)   # the annotation is required
```

A direct request to such an endpoint is 409.

## Rules

- Recognize the requests of the consumer only with `is_internal_request(scope)`
  (`SCOPE_INTERNAL_KEY` in the ASGI scope, which clients cannot set). Never trust a
  header: `X-Async-Background-Internal` is ignored.
- Only JSON bodies (an object or a list of objects) are queued: another body (multipart,
  form, binary) is replayed as `{}`.
- The queued request keeps all headers, `Authorization` included, in the Kafka topic; it
  runs with the client's token, so the token must still be valid when the consumer runs it.
- Requests with the same `data.id` in the body go to the same Kafka partition.
- WebSocket requests and the results route are never queued.

agents_md:
# bazis-notify — guide for AI agents

Stored notifications of the users: `notify` creates a row per recipient (the text in his
language), the client lists, reads and deletes his own notifications through the API, and
the new ones are delivered live to the open sessions (with bazis-ws) and by e-mail
(`email=True`). Use it for anything a user must see even if he was offline: reminders,
deadlines, results of background work, billing events.

### The sections

Read a section with `package_guide("bazis-notify", "<section>")` when the step at hand
needs it; `guide_search` finds the part of a section that answers a question. Notifying
users needs Setup, Notification types, Creating notifications and Rules.

| Section | Read it when |
|---|---|
| Setup | you install it: the app, the router, live delivery with bazis-ws, the retention setting |
| Notification types | you declare the types: `register` in `<app>/notifications.py`, category, severity, action |
| Creating notifications | the code notifies users: `notify`, the texts per recipient, `dedupe_key`, `metadata`, the commit; every user at once (`notify_all`) |
| Live delivery (bazis-ws) | a client gets them live: the messages on the socket |
| E-mail | a notification is also mailed (`email=True`) |
| API | a client lists, reads and deletes the notifications of its user |
| Retention | old notifications are deleted (`delete_expired`) |
| Rules | before you write the code, once |

## Setup

- `BS_INSTALLED_APPS` gets `bazis.contrib.notify` (a Django app: run `migrate`). It needs
  bazis-users (the user of the request, `UserLanguageMixin.language` for the texts).
- Register the API in the router module of the project (`BS_BAZIS_ROUTER_MODULE`):

  ```python
  router = BazisRouter(prefix='/api/v1')
  router.register('bazis.contrib.notify.router')   # /api/v1/notify/notification/
  ```

- Live delivery (optional): install `bazis-notify[ws]` (bazis-ws), give the user model
  `UserWsMixin` and register `bazis.contrib.ws.router` (see the guide of bazis-ws).
  Without them the notifications are stored (and e-mailed) only.
- Setting: `BS_BAZIS_NOTIFY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default empty: kept forever), see Retention.

## Notification types

Each notification has a registered type. Declare the types of an app in
`<app>/notifications.py` (imported when the apps are ready):

```python
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from bazis.contrib.notify.registry import register

register('billing.purchase_declined', title=_('Purchase declined'), severity='error',
         action={'route': '/settings/billing'})
register('training.deadline', title=_('Deadline soon'), severity='warning')
```

- The slug is lowercase words joined by dots; `category` defaults to its first part
  (`billing`), `severity` is `info` (default), `success`, `warning` or `error`, `action` is
  the default action of its notifications. The API shows `category` and `severity` from
  the type: no conditions on the type in the model or the client.
- `notify` with a type that is not registered raises `UnknownNotificationTypeError`; the same
  slug registered differently raises `ImproperlyConfigured`. A notification whose type is
  no longer registered is still listed (category: the first part of its type, `info`).

## Creating notifications

```python
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from bazis.contrib.notify.service import notify

# in hook_after_create / hook_after_update of a route, a transit, a task
notify(
    order.customer,                       # a user or an iterable (None and repeats skipped)
    'billing.purchase_declined',
    _('Payment for %(product)s declined'),   # title: a template, translated per recipient
    _('No credits were charged.'),           # body (optional)
    params={'product': order.product.name},
    action={'route': f'/orders/{order.pk}'},  # optional, the action of the type otherwise
    metadata={'order_id': str(order.pk)},     # optional data for the client
    dedupe_key=f'declined:{order.pk}',        # optional: at most one per user and key
    email=True,                               # optional: also by e-mail
)
```

- The texts are rendered for each recipient inside `in_user_language(user)` of bazis-users
  (`user.language`, else LANGUAGE_CODE): a lazy string is translated there, then formatted with `params` (`%`);
  a function `lambda user: ...` is called with the user and gives the final text (`params`
  are not applied to it, so a `%` in the data of the user is safe). Do not format a lazy string
  before the call (`_('...') % {...}` is translated in the language of the request).
  The rows keep the rendered texts.
- `notify` returns the notifications it created (loaded back, ordinary instances). With
  `dedupe_key`, a user who already has a notification with that key gets none (no
  e-mail, no message on the socket): a retried call or task does not notify twice. The
  key holds while the notification exists: after a DELETE, `clear` or the retention
  deleted it, the same key notifies again (make the key say what it is about, e.g. the
  object and its version). One insert for all the recipients.
- `action` and `metadata` are JSON (lazy strings and dates are converted). The keys of
  `metadata` containing `token`, `secret`, `password`, `receipt`, `authorization`,
  `api_key`, `apikey`, `credential`, `cookie` or `traceback` are dropped at any depth; the
  user sees the metadata, never put private data there.
- A notification is not edited: a write that changes anything but `read_at` fails
  (`validate_item`). Delete it and create another.
- The delivery waits for the commit of the current transaction (at once outside one): a
  rolled back write delivers nothing.

### Every user (fan-out)

`notify_all(users, type, title, body, batch_size=500, **kwargs)` takes a queryset (read
with `iterator()`) or an iterable and calls `notify` per batch: one insert and a constant
number of queries per batch, whatever the number of users. Run it from a task of bazis-bg
outside a transaction, so that each batch commits and is delivered on its own; with a
`dedupe_key`, a retried task skips the users already notified:

```python
from bazis.contrib.bg.basic.base import BgBase
from bazis.contrib.notify.service import notify_all

class Announce(BgBase):
    name = 'Announce a release'
    is_transaction = False

    def __init__(self, release_id):
        self.release_id = release_id

    def handle(self):
        users = User.objects.filter(is_active=True)
        self.set_result({'created': notify_all(
            users, 'product.release', _('Version %(version)s is out'),
            params={'version': ...}, dedupe_key=f'release:{self.release_id}')})
```

Not one task per user, and no `exists()` per user: the deduplication key does that.

## Live delivery (bazis-ws)

After the commit, to the channel of each recipient whose user model has `UserWsMixin` (the
message arrives as `{"type": "data", "data": "<JSON>"}`, see bazis-ws):

- `{"action": "notification_created", "notification": {...}, "unread_count": N}`: the new
  notification with the attributes of its resource (`id`, `notification_type`, `title`,
  `body`, `action`, `metadata`, `category`, `severity`, `is_read`, `read_at`,
  `dt_created`) and the unread count of the user;
- `{"action": "notifications_changed", "unread_count": N}`: after a read, an unread, a
  delete (one or `clear`) or `read_all` of the user (through the API or `read_all`/`clear`
  of the service); the client refetches its list.

A failed publish (Redis down) is logged (`bazis.contrib.notify.service`) and does not fail
the write; the notification stays stored. A client fetches the unread notifications when
it (re)connects: the socket delivers only while it is connected.

## E-mail

`email=True` sends each created notification to `user.email` (users without one are
skipped): the subject is the title (on one line), the text the body (the title without a
body), in the language of the user, from `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`. The messages of one
`notify` call go after the commit through one connection of the default mailer of the project,
which the core configures from the dynamic settings `BAZIS_EMAIL_BACKEND` (default
`bazis.core.mail.DynamicSMTPEmailBackend`), `BAZIS_EMAIL_HOST`, `BAZIS_EMAIL_PORT`,
`BAZIS_EMAIL_HOST_USER`, `BAZIS_EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD`, `BAZIS_EMAIL_USE_TLS`,
`BAZIS_EMAIL_USE_SSL` (`BS_BAZIS_EMAIL_*`, editable in the admin) and `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL`.
Each message is sent on its own: a refused address (or one the backend cannot encode) is
logged with the notification and the user (`bazis.contrib.notify.service`) and the others
are sent; a mail server that cannot be reached is logged by Django (the failed `on_commit`
callback). Neither fails the write. The sending runs in the process of the write: send to many users
from a task (`notify_all`), not in a request. Tests get the messages in `mail.outbox`
(Django uses the locmem backend in tests).

## API

`/api/v1/notify/notification/` (the resource `notify.notification`), only the
notifications of the user of the request; another user's notification is 404, a
request without a valid token 401 (`UserRequiredRouteBase` of bazis-users).

- `GET /`: the list, newest first, with the JSON:API filters and pagination:
  `filter=is_read=false` (the unread ones, e.g. on (re)connect), `filter=notification_type=billing.purchase_declined`,
  `page[limit]`, `page[offset]`. `GET /{id}/`: one notification.
- `PATCH /{id}/` with `{"data": {"id", "type": "notify.notification", "attributes":
  {"read_at": "<any time>"}}}` marks it read, `"read_at": null` unread; the time is the
  server's (the value sent is not stored; a read notification keeps its time); any other
  attribute is 422. `DELETE /{id}/` deletes it. No create: notifications come from `notify`.
- `GET /unread_count/` → `{"unread_count": N}`; `POST /read_all/` → `{"read": N}`;
  `POST /clear/` (deletes all) → `{"deleted": N}`.
- Attributes: `notification_type`, `title`, `body`, `action`, `metadata`, `read_at`,
  `dt_created`, `is_read`, `category`, `severity`. The recipient and the deduplication key
  are not shown.

## Retention

`delete_expired(days=None, batch_size=1000)` deletes the notifications created more than
`BAZIS_NOTIFY_RETENTION_DAYS` days ago (read or not; `days` overrides the setting; nothing
without either) and returns their number. It deletes `batch_size` rows per statement (by
the index of `dt_created`): outside a transaction each batch commits on its own. The
deleted keys no longer deduplicate. Run it daily from a periodic task of bazis-bg
(a `BgBase` whose `handle` calls it, with a `TaskCron` such as `"0 3 * * *"`).

## Rules

- Create notifications only with `notify`/`notify_all` (types, rendering, deduplication,
  delivery); not with `Notification.objects.create`.
- Notify only the users who may see what the notification says.
- Not from `validate_item`: it may run more than once for one write; use the hooks of the
  write, a transit or a task.
- `bazis.contrib.ws.messages.notify` of bazis-ws stays a live message without storage
  (lost if the user is not connected); use this package for what the user must find later.

package.name: bazis-front
package.summary: the frontend layer of a Bazis product (pre-release): a React + TypeScript + Vite frontend made from a template, with the contract and its TypeScript generated from the backend, the protocol client copied into it, and the specs of the product validated against the contract
solves: a typed frontend of a Bazis backend whose contract is generated from its OpenAPI
the resources, roles and transits of the backend as one generated contract.json for the frontend and AI agents
the JSON:API protocol of Bazis in TypeScript: filters, errors, pagination, login, permission meta, transits, uploads
a new frontend next to the backend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite 7, TanStack Query, Tailwind 4 with shadcn/ui
the product described as specs (roles, entities, access, scenarios, screens, design) and checked against the backend: missing resources, fields, transits and permissions of the roles

extension_points.name: manage.py bazis_front
extension_points.use_when: create the frontend of the product with `bazis_front init` (frontend/ with the copied client and its lock, and the starters of spec/); export the contract with `bazis_front contract` (contract/openapi.json, contract/contract.json and frontend/src/bazis/generated/), `--check` only compares; validate spec/ against the contract with `bazis_front check` (`--json`, exit 1 on errors); copy the components with `bazis_front add`; generate the end-to-end tests of the scenarios with `bazis_front e2e` (`--check` only compares); compile spec/design/ into the theme of the frontend with `bazis_front design` (`--check` only compares); after `pip install -U bazis-front`, bring the copies to the new version with `bazis_front update` (a three-way merge with the changes of the product, `--check` only lists them); see the copies, the generated files and every stale or changed one with `bazis_front status` (`--json`, writes nothing)

pitfalls.text: the contract (contract/openapi.json, contract/contract.json) is generated: export it again after every change of the backend, never edit it

the permit roles and the statusy transits of the contract are read from the database: export from a migrated database (`migrate` applies the roles, statuses and transits declared in roles.py and workflow.py)

frontend/src/bazis/generated/ (contract.ts, schema.d.ts) is written by `bazis_front contract`, never by hand; schema.d.ts needs Node and the `npm install` of the frontend, otherwise it is `missing` in the lock and `contract --check` fails

the specs (spec/) are checked against contract/contract.json: export the contract before `bazis_front check`; `access` must be covered by the permissions of the permit roles (P019), and the issues have stable codes (the section "The issues of check" of AGENTS.md)

the theme of the frontend (frontend/src/bazis/generated/theme.css and theme.ts) is compiled from spec/design/ by `bazis_front design` (and `init`): generate it again after every change of the design and after `bazis_front update`, never edit it; colors, radii and fonts of the screens come from its tokens (Tailwind classes such as `bg-primary`, `bg-success-soft`), never literal colors

the screens in frontend/src/screens/generated/ (their routes, the navigation, the texts of the specs) are written by `bazis_front screens` (and `init`) from spec/, never by hand: generate them again after every change of the specs (and after the `bazis_front update` of a frontend made before them, which has none); what a spec cannot say goes to an extension (`extend`, src/screens/<id>/extend.tsx) or a custom screen (`custom`, src/screens/<id>/index.tsx); a generated file edited since is not overwritten without `--force`

the assets follow the protocol of recent Bazis packages: bazis-ws>=2.5.0 (the socket is open at `subscribed`), bazis-authing>=2.6.0 (the logout), bazis-permit>=2.7.0 (the selectors, the filters restricted to the fields the user sees), bazis-statusy>=2.13.0 (the translated payload schemas, the initial status of each model, the transits of the items of a list), bazis-uploadable>=2.7.0 (the files of their author, their download route), bazis-bg>=2.6.0 (the download of the file of a task); an older installed package is the warning front.W006 (the error C004 of `bazis_front check`): upgrade it
the client in frontend/src/bazis/client/ is a copy kept pristine for the updates of bazis-front: wrap it in src/app/, do not edit it

after `pip install -U bazis-front` the copies in frontend/ are of the old version until `bazis_front update` merges the new one with the changes of the product; it fails with conflict markers in the files that both changed (resolve them, then tsc and npm test: tsc finds the markers left in .ts/.tsx only, `update --check` and front.W004 in every file of the conflicts until they are gone), and `add` refuses until then; commit frontend/.bazis/ (the pristine copies the merge needs) and the lock

a copy of bazis-front changed in frontend/ (a file of src/bazis/ or e2e/bazis/ whose hash differs from bazis-front.lock.json) is merged by `bazis_front update` with every new version, a change of the same lines by both is a conflict: never edit the client, the hooks, the i18n or the helpers; change a component through its props or a component of the product that composes it
frontend/e2e/generated/shots.ts is written by `bazis_front shots` from the specs, never by hand: take the screenshots again after a change of the screens, the scenarios or the design

the screens are done when `bazis_front shots` (the backend and the frontend running, E2E_PASSWORD set) reports no error in frontend/.scratch/shots/report.json (a page that scrolls sideways on a phone, a raw name or a UUID shown, a text without contrast, a screen not reached) and the screenshots pass the checklist of the guide: fix the specs, the screens or the backend and take them again, at most three rounds; the errors left after them, or screenshots never taken (no report), are the warning front.W009, not a stale part of the frontend; .scratch/ is never committed

bazis-ws keeps nothing: a message published before the page subscribed is lost; publish after the commit, and the hooks refetch every query after a reconnect; the notifications of bazis-ws alone are those of the session, the stored ones are bazis-notify (notify of bazis.contrib.notify.service, which delivers them live itself: never publish them a second time with bazis-ws; the bell lists them with useInbox)

the file URL of an uploaded file (bazis-uploadable) or of a task (bazis-bg) is served by the media host to anyone who has it: never link it; the frontend reads the content with the token from <path><id>/download/ (useDownload, FileValue, TaskProgress)

the common channel of bazis-ws reaches every user session (anonymous ones with BAZIS_WS_ANONYMOUS_COMMON_CHANNEL): it is not for data, publish only the invalidation hint {"resource": "<type>"} there, the ids and the notifications only to the users who may see the item (notify of bazis.contrib.ws.messages in bazis-ws 2.6.0, user.ws_publish before)

bazis-uploadable gives a user only his own files, and the core (2.7) links and includes only the objects the user may see: a relationship to the file of another user is 403 ERR_RELATION_ACCESS (no check of its own in the route set, which must know the user: UserRouteBase or a route set of bazis-permit), and include leaves the file out; FileValue shows it as not available

the frontend is in the languages of the backend (LANGUAGES, LANGUAGE_CODE): every text of a screen goes through t() of @/bazis/i18n with a key of the dictionaries of the product (src/i18n/<language>.ts, merged over those of the components), dates and numbers through its Intl formatters; the backend translates with gettext (its catalogs made, filled and compiled by manage.py bazis_messages: make, the translations in a JSON file kept in the project, apply; .po and .mo committed) and the translated fields of its data (the names of roles, statuses and transits in every language: English gettext_lazy names in roles.py and workflow.py translated by the catalogs, with bazis-permit and bazis-statusy 2.9; the roles of bazis-permit before 2.9 set in the data migrations)

the contract knows the socket of bazis-ws only when it is routed in the router module (router.register('bazis.contrib.ws.router') with bazis-ws 2.6.0, under the prefix of the router; router.routes.append(ws_route) before, /ws) or on the application of BAZIS_APP_MODULE; registered only in the main module, CAPABILITIES.ws.path is null and the frontend opens no socket
without Kafka bazis-async-request runs a request with X-Async-Background at once and answers as usual: the frontend takes both the 202 with a task and the response

a choice is shown, offered and filtered by its label: the runtime schemas give the labels of the choices of a model field (enumDict, translated with gettext_lazy) and the components use them; never make a model of the choices for their labels, nor map the values to texts in the frontend; the scenarios fill and expect the label

an item added from the card of its parent fixes the relationship: RelatedList of resource-card (card.related of the spec) or ResourceForm fixed={{<relation>: id}} (useResourceForm(path, {fixed})), never a form of the product that sets the value in an effect

`manage.py e2e_data` runs before every run of the end-to-end tests and only adds: it never deletes a user or a record (of the previous runs, of the scenarios, its own), finds its records by a key of their own, creates those that are missing and sets their dates and the password again; the scenarios count only the records of `e2e_data` and change only the items they create (P033), find them by their ids (`created` of the helpers) and the notifications since their start, since the items of the runs pile up
the frontend is not a security boundary: permissions are checked by the backend, the frontend only reads the permission meta and the runtime schemas

a point of a model is a PointField (GeoJSON [lon, lat] in the API, `format: point` in the contract, `type: point` in the specs), never two float fields: the components show and edit it, `bazis_front add map` gives the maps (Leaflet, set in package.json: run npm install); declare it geography=True; the default tiles of MapProvider are OpenStreetMap for development: set the tiles of the product and its CSP in production; a list of what is near filters with nearFilter and sorts with nearSort, the nearest first

a custom action of a route set (`@http_post('/export/')`, kind `other` in the contract) is called with useAction of @/bazis/react (client.action), never with fetch: the client sends the token and the language, its errors are ApiError (the errors of its body by field: bodyErrors()), and the id of a task of bazis-bg that it answers with is shown by TaskProgress; an action declared with GET that a screen shows is read with useActionQuery or useItemActionQuery (a query refetched with its resource), never a react-query wrapper of your own

agents_md:
# bazis-front — guide for AI agents

The frontend layer of a product on Bazis: a React + TypeScript + Vite frontend next to the
backend, whose contract is generated from the backend and whose protocol code is copied
from this package. There are no npm packages of Bazis: the TypeScript code of the package
is shipped as package data and copied into the product, which then owns the copy.

**Status: pre-release.** The package ships `manage.py bazis_front init` (a frontend made
from its template, with the protocol client, the React hooks and the first components
copied into it, and the starters of the specs), `manage.py bazis_front add` (the
components), `manage.py bazis_front contract` (the export of the contract and the
TypeScript generated from it), `manage.py bazis_front check` (the validation of the
specs against the contract), `manage.py bazis_front design` (the theme of the frontend
compiled from the design of the specs), `manage.py bazis_front e2e` (the Playwright tests of
the scenarios of the specs) and `manage.py bazis_front update` (the copies brought to a new
version of bazis-front, merged with the changes of the product).

### Setup

`pip install bazis-front` (needs bazis 2.17.0 or newer: the aggregates of the lists, which the
tiles and the charts of the dashboards read) and add `"bazis.contrib.front"` to
`BS_INSTALLED_APPS`. The assets follow the protocol of recent versions of the packages of
the capabilities: bazis-ws 2.5.0 (the socket is open once the server sends `subscribed`),
bazis-authing 2.6.0 (the logout endpoint), bazis-permit 2.7.0 (the selectors of the
contract, also many-to-many and reverse relations, and the filter of a route restricted to
the fields the user sees), bazis-statusy 2.13.0 (the JSON Schemas of the transit payloads
with their titles translated, the initial status of each model, `Workflow(initial=...)`, and
the transits of the items of a list, `for_transit`, which the boards read),
bazis-uploadable 2.7.0 (the files of their author, for every route, and their download
route with its access check), bazis-bg 2.6.0 (the download route of the file of a task).
An older one that the project installs is the warning
`front.W006` of the system checks (it does not block `migrate`; `front.W002` does not repeat
it) and the error `C004` of `bazis_front check`: like any error of the specs, it also stops
`bazis_front e2e` (no tests are generated) and the comparison of `front.W003` until the
package is upgraded.

### Building the frontend of a product

The steps, each with the sections to read when you reach it, not before. Read a section with
`package_guide("bazis-front", "<section>")`; `guide_search` finds the section that answers a
question, and the `API:` sections give the signature of every export of the copied code (the
props of the components, the hooks, the client, the helpers of the tests), so that the copies
in `frontend/` never need to be read.

1. Install bazis-front and the packages of the product (above), then create the frontend
   with `python manage.py bazis_front init` (`--preset portal` for a product for the public,
   `workspace` for the staff): "The frontend".
2. Describe the product top down: `spec/product.yaml` (the roles with their `test_user`, or
   `anonymous: true` for the users who do not log in, the entities with their fields,
   workflows and access, the scenarios, the languages), "The
   specs"; then a file `spec/screens/<id>.yaml` per screen (the home, `/`, a dashboard:
   fill the starter of `init`) and the design, "The specs of the screens and the design".
3. Build the backend to satisfy the specs: the models and route sets, the roles with their
   permissions in `roles.py`, the workflows in `workflow.py`, the `e2e_data` command, "The
   backend of a product" (and the guides of bazis-permit and bazis-statusy).
4. Migrate the database and export the contract, `python manage.py bazis_front contract`:
   "The contract".
5. Run `python manage.py bazis_front check` and fix the spec or the backend as the hint of
   each issue says until it reports no errors, exporting the contract again after every
   change of the backend: "The issues of check".
6. Generate the screens, `python manage.py bazis_front screens` (it copies the components
   that they import), and write what their specs cannot say in their extensions (`extend`)
   or the screens that they do not fit (`custom: true`) in `frontend/src/screens/<id>/` (as
   "The specs of the screens and the design" says): "The components", "Writing the screens" and "Composing beyond
   the specs"; by topic "Choices, filters, permissions and relationships", "Files, points and
   maps", "Custom actions and background work", "The socket" and "The language"; the data
   through "The hooks" and "The client".
7. Design the product: choose the palette, the fonts, the shape and the surface of
   `spec/design/theme.yaml` for its domain, the icon of every entity and the tones of the
   statuses, then generate the theme, `python manage.py bazis_front design`: "The design".
8. Generate the end-to-end tests, `python manage.py bazis_front e2e`, and run them with
   `npm run e2e` against the migrated backend with the data of `e2e_data`: "The end-to-end
   tests".
9. Take the screenshots, `python manage.py bazis_front shots` (the backend running as for
   `npm run e2e`), read `frontend/.scratch/shots/report.json` and look at the screenshots,
   fix every error and take them again, at most three rounds: "The visual check".
10. Check the frontend in `frontend/`: `npm run format`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`,
   `npm test` and `npm run build`; after the last edit of a file run `npm run format` and
   `npm run lint` again; `python manage.py bazis_front status` lists what is stale.

Later, after `pip install -U bazis-front`: "Updating the copies".

### Rules

- **Generate the contract, never write it.** `contract/` and
  `frontend/src/bazis/generated/` come from `manage.py bazis_front contract`. Generate
  them again after every change of the backend and fix what the compiler reports; do not
  edit the generated files and do not declare resource types by hand.
- **Describe the product in `spec/` and keep `bazis_front check` green.** Build the
  backend to satisfy the specs (models, route sets, and the roles with their permissions,
  the statuses and the transits declared in `roles.py` and `workflow.py`), export the
  contract, and fix every issue that `check` reports, in the spec or in the backend, as its
  hint says.
- **Use the hooks and the client, do not reimplement them.** Data of the backend is read
  and changed with the hooks (`@/bazis/react`); requests, filters, errors, pagination,
  authentication and permission checks go through the client. Do not edit the copies;
  extend them with wrappers in the product code, so that a new version replaces them
  without conflicts.
- **The backend decides the permissions.** Do not encode roles or permission rules in the
  frontend. Hide or disable controls from what the backend reports: the permission meta
  and the runtime schema `schema_update` of the item.
- **Compose the screens from the components, own them.** Components and screens are part
  of the product and may be changed freely; keep the contract tests of the components
  passing, since the scenarios act through their `data-bz`.
- **Design through the tokens, never with literal colors.** The look of the product is
  `spec/design/` compiled by `bazis_front design`: a brand is a change of the tokens, not of
  the components; the screens use the Tailwind classes of the tokens (`bg-primary`,
  `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-success-soft`) and the patterns of the preset (`Screen`,
  `ListCardLayout`, `FormSurface`, the components), never colors such as `bg-blue-600` or
  `#3b82f6`.
- **Generate the screens, never edit them.** `bazis_front screens` writes
  `frontend/src/screens/generated/` from the specs: run it after every change of `spec/`;
  what a spec cannot say goes to a custom screen (`custom`) or an extension (`extend`), never
  into the generated files.
- **Generate the end-to-end tests, never edit them.** Run `bazis_front e2e` after every
  change of the scenarios or the screens of the specs and keep `npm run e2e` green against
  the migrated backend with the data of `manage.py e2e_data`; write the other tests in
  `frontend/e2e/custom/`.
- **Look at the screens, not only at the tests.** After the screens, `bazis_front shots`
  checks what they render on a desktop and a phone, in the light and the dark mode; fix its
  errors and the checklist of the screenshots before the screens are done.

### The sections

| Section | Read it when |
|---|---|
| The frontend | you create the frontend (`init`), need the files of `frontend/` and who changes them, the npm commands, the lock, `status` |
| The specs | you write `spec/product.yaml`: the roles, entities, fields, workflows, access (with the permissions it requires), scenarios and their steps |
| The specs of the screens and the design | you write `spec/screens/<id>.yaml` (list, card, form, dashboard, board, calendar, `card.related`, `card.tabs`, `list.filter`, `list.map`, `list.bulk`, the custom actions), which primitive a part of the product takes, the `data-bz` marks, `spec/design/theme.yaml` |
| The issues of check | `bazis_front check` reports a code (`C…`, `P…`, `S…`, `D…`) |
| The backend of a product | you build the backend the frontend relies on: the declared roles and workflows, the test data, the changes and the notifications, the invariants, the labels |
| The contract | you export the contract or read `contract.json` and `contract.ts` (`ROUTES`, `CAPABILITIES`, the sections of the capabilities) |
| The components | you choose the components and copy them (`add`): what each one is, its `data-bz`, what it requires |
| Writing the screens | you generate the screens (`bazis_front screens`) or write a custom one from its spec: the component of each part of a spec, the routes, the navigation, the card next to the list |
| Composing beyond the specs | a screen needs more than the specs say: a section of your own, a form of your own (and the marks that the tests need), numbers and dates in a text |
| Choices, filters, permissions and relationships | the choices and their labels, the related items ("add here"), the filters of a list, the navigation, the field permissions, the pickers and the labels of related items, the to-many fields in a form |
| Files, points and maps | the files of bazis-uploadable, the points and the maps, what is near |
| Custom actions and background work | an action of the backend that is no CRUD (an export, a report), its permission, a task of bazis-bg, a background request |
| The socket | bazis-ws: the live updates, the notifications and the bell, the protocol of the socket |
| The design | the presets, the top bar, the tokens, the brand, the dark mode, the tones of the statuses, the classes of the theme |
| The end-to-end tests | `bazis_front e2e`, the steps and their helpers, `e2e_data`, `npm run e2e` and its ports, the tests of your own |
| The visual check | `bazis_front shots`: the screenshots, their report and its codes (`V…`), the checklist of the screenshots, when the screens are done |
| The client | a request that the hooks do not cover, the filters, the errors of a form, the permission meta, the uploads |
| The hooks | the data of the backend in a screen: lists, items, forms, schemas, permissions, transits, uploads, the socket, tasks |
| The language | the languages, the dictionaries and `t()`, the formats of dates and numbers, the language of the profile |
| Logins with bazis-authing | the login of the template with bazis-users or bazis-authing, the sign-out |
| Protocol facts that are easy to get wrong | a request is refused or answers otherwise than you expected: the filters, `include`, 403 and 404, the errors, the files, the points, the tasks |
| Updating the copies | after `pip install -U bazis-front`: `update`, its conflicts, the changes of the API of the copies |
| `API: …` (generated) | you need the props of a component, the parameters and the result of a hook or of the client, a helper of the end-to-end tests |

## The frontend

```bash
python manage.py bazis_front init                  # create frontend/ in the product root and run `npm install`
python manage.py bazis_front init --no-node        # the same without `npm install`
python manage.py bazis_front init --preset portal  # the starters of the design of the preset portal (workspace by default)
python manage.py bazis_front screens               # the screens of the specs in src/screens/generated/
python manage.py bazis_front screens --check       # fails when they differ from the specs (CI)
```

`init` creates `frontend/` next to `manage.py`, a React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7 app with
TanStack Query, React Router 7 and Tailwind 4 set up for shadcn/ui (`components.json`),
with the layout of the application (`app-shell`), a login screen (`login-form`) and the
screens of the specs. It never overwrites an existing `frontend/`. It writes:

- `spec/` next to `manage.py`, when the product has none (an existing one is kept): the
  JSON Schemas of the specs in `spec/schema/` (for the editors) and starters of
  `spec/product.yaml`, `spec/screens/home.yaml` (the home, a dashboard at `/` without
  tiles: the product has no entity to count yet) and `spec/design/theme.yaml` and
  `spec/design/tokens.json` (those of the preset of `--preset`); see [The specs](#the-specs);
- the theme of the frontend, `src/bazis/generated/fonts.css`, `theme.css` and `theme.ts`, compiled from
  `spec/design/` as `bazis_front design` does (see [The design](#the-design)); a design with
  errors is reported and the theme is left to `bazis_front design`;
- the screens of the specs, as `bazis_front screens` generates them (see
  [Writing the screens](#writing-the-screens)), with the components that they import; specs
  with errors are reported and left to `bazis_front screens`;

- the files of the template (`assets/template`), which the product owns from then on
  (`update` merges a new version with its changes), among them `frontend/AGENTS.md`, which
  points the agents to the sections of this guide, with their pristine copy in
  `.bazis/base/template@<version>/`;
- the protocol client in `src/bazis/client/` and the React hooks in `src/bazis/react/`,
  each file stamped with `// bazis-front <version> asset <asset>` after its license header,
  and the same pristine copy in `.bazis/base/<asset>@<version>/` for the merge of later
  versions. The hooks of a package are copied only when the product has it at `init` (its
  app in `INSTALLED_APPS`, as the capabilities of the contract): with bazis-statusy the
  asset `react-statusy` in `src/bazis/react/statusy/`, with bazis-uploadable `react-uploadable`
  in `src/bazis/react/uploadable/`, with bazis-ws `react-ws` in `src/bazis/react/ws/` (bazis-ws
  is not a Django app: its installed package is enough), with bazis-bg `react-bg` in
  `src/bazis/react/bg/`, with bazis-async-background `react-async` in
  `src/bazis/react/async/`. A package installed after `init` has
  no hooks in the frontend until `bazis_front add react-statusy` (or a component that
  requires them) copies them: `check` reports it (`C003`);
- the translation of the interface in `src/bazis/i18n/` (the asset `i18n`, copied like the
  hooks; see [The language](#the-language));
- the components that the template uses, `state-panel`, `app-shell` and `login-form`, in
  the same way, with the shadcn/ui components they use (see [The components](#the-components));
- the helpers of the end-to-end tests in `e2e/bazis/` (the asset `playwright`, copied like
  the hooks), with `playwright.config.ts` and `e2e/custom/` of the template (see
  [The end-to-end tests](#the-end-to-end-tests));
- `bazis-front.lock.json`: the hashes of the generated files and of the OpenAPI they were
  made from (see below), and the version and the file hashes of every copied asset, the
  template too; an asset that was not copied is not in it.
  `bazis_front e2e` adds the hashes of the specs and of the tests it generates (`e2e`),
  `init` and `bazis_front design` those of the design and of the theme (`design`), `init`
  and `bazis_front screens` those of the specs and of the screens (`screens`).

Commit `bazis-front.lock.json` and `.bazis/`: `update` merges a new version with the
changes of the product from the pristine copies, and the old version is no longer installed
then. The files that `init` and `add` copy are
listed in `assets/registry.json` of the package. The frontend compiles once `contract` has generated
`src/bazis/generated/`. It has a login only when the backend has bazis-users; without it
every screen is open and requests are anonymous. The login is the token endpoint of
bazis-users, or with bazis-authing its services: the username and the password through the
service `password`, and a button for each service whose page opens in a window (Google);
see [Logins with bazis-authing](#logins-with-bazis-authing).

The files of the frontend and of the product, by the layers of bazis-front, and who changes
them:
